llm_summary: Researchers examined whether elderly patients aged 75 and older with kidney failure live longer after receiving a kidney transplant from a deceased donor compared to staying on dialysis, which is a treatment that filters waste from the blood using a machine. The study used data from a national transplant registry between 2015 and 2023, analyzing information from 2,670 patients to simulate what would happen in a fair comparison between the two treatment options. They found that transplant recipients faced a higher risk of death in the first three months after surgery, but those who survived this early period lived significantly longer than patients who continued dialysis, with a survival advantage of about 111 days by the five-year mark. The survival benefit only became clear after about three years, meaning patients need to survive the initial risky period to gain the long-term advantage of transplantation. These findings suggest that age alone should not prevent elderly patients from considering kidney transplantation, and doctors should have detailed conversations with patients about both the early risks and the later survival benefits to help them make informed decisions about their treatment.

title: Impaired cerebral autoregulation in patients with moyamoya disease and moyamoya syndrome: A prospective cross-sectional study.
abstract: Moyamoya disease and syndrome (MMDS) are rare cerebrovascular etiologies defined by stenosis of the distal intracranial internal carotid artery and proximal branches, with secondary development of small-vessel collaterals. Current techniques to characterize MMDS severity generally provide measurements in resting conditions (degree of stenosis, vessel collateralization, and regional oxygen delivery). In addition, some measurements of cerebral perfusion are performed with induced hypercapnia or acetazolamide to assess chemoreactivity. Despite the battery of exams, current techniques do not provide information about cerebral autoregulation. This study aimed to investigate dysfunction of cerebral autoregulation among patients with MMDS. Metrics of cerebral autoregulation were determined by transfer function analysis (TFA) of Middle Cerebral Artery velocities obtained with transcranial doppler ultrasound. Fourteen adult patients with MMDS and fifteen healthy, age- and sex-matched controls were included. Metrics of TFA (gain, phase, and coherence) were obtained within three frequency ranges (very low frequency (0.02-0.07 Hz), low frequency (0.07-0.2 Hz), and high frequency (0.2-0.5 Hz), in alignment with recommendations from the International Cerebral Autoregulation Research Network. Compared to the control group, the MMDS group had a significantly lower, very low frequency phase (P = 0.005), low frequency phase (P < 0.001), and high frequency phase (P = 0.010). In addition, the MMDS group had a significantly lower, low frequency coherence (P = 0.033). Regression analyses demonstrated a significant association between Suzuki grade and low frequency gain (m=-0.283, R2=0.089, P = 0.045) and high frequency gain (m=-0.338, R2=0.115, P = 0.026). Among patients with MMDS, there was a significant association between breath-hold index and low frequency phase (m=11.78, R2=0.171, P = 0.045), low frequency coherence (m=0.08, R2=0.242, P = 0.015), and high frequency coherence (m=0.06, R2=0.380, P = 0.001). Overall, these findings highlight a notable impairment in cerebral autoregulation in MMDS that appears to be associated with disease severity. Further studies are needed to assess whether cerebral autoregulation predicts disease progression and outcomes after surgical revascularization in MMDS patients.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. llm_summary: Moyamoya disease and syndrome are rare blood vessel disorders where arteries in the brain become narrowed, and the body tries to compensate by growing tiny replacement vessels, but doctors currently lack good ways to measure how well the brain can adjust its blood flow in response to changing conditions. Researchers compared fourteen patients with this disease to fifteen healthy people of similar age and sex, using ultrasound to measure blood flow in the brain's middle cerebral artery while analyzing how the brain's blood vessels responded to different frequencies of blood pressure changes. The patients with moyamoya disease showed significantly weaker responses across all frequency ranges tested, meaning their brains were less able to automatically regulate blood flow the way healthy brains do. The severity of the disease, measured by a standard grading system, was linked to how poorly the brain could adjust its blood flow, suggesting that worse disease correlates with worse autoregulation problems. The researchers conclude that this impaired ability to regulate blood flow appears to be an important feature of moyamoya disease that may help predict how the disease will progress and whether surgery to restore blood flow will help patients.

title: The eye sees what the mind knows: Eye tracking and artificial intelligence to assess surgical resident level of expertise.
abstract: Surgical education continues to strive to move beyond traditional time-based competency metrics. As gaze behaviors can reflect underlying cognitive strategies, eye-tracking technology may provide insight into individual differences. Hence, we sought to characterize gaze-based phenotypes in surgical learners to examine their relationship with training level.We conducted an eye-tracking study involving general surgery residents from postgraduate year 1 through postgraduate year 5 using screen-based eye trackers. Gaze patterns were collected on 2 30-second video clips of operations. Three core metrics were extracted: average dwell time per fixation, spatial dispersion, and scan entropy. Principal component analysis was applied for dimensionality reduction, followed by k-means clustering to identify distinct visual learning phenotypes.Fifty-seven residents participated in this study. Principal component analysis identified 3 components explaining 87.7% of the variance in gaze behavior, with scan entropy and spatial dispersion being primary drivers. K-means clustering revealed 3 gaze phenotypes: (1) focused-stable-systematic, characterized by long, deliberate fixations, low spatial dispersion, and systematic scan paths. This expert-like pattern was predominantly noted among postgraduate year 4-5 residents; (2) brief-stable-systematic, defined by brief fixations but similarly low dispersion and entropy, suggesting a structured but superficial approach. This pattern was common among postgraduate year 1-3 residents; and (3) brief-active-exploratory, marked by high scan entropy and broad spatial dispersion. This phenotype was exclusively composed of postgraduate year 1-2 residents.Gaze-based phenotypes capture meaningful cognitive strategies in surgical learners that are not fully explained by postgraduate year level. Identification of these visual learning profiles offers a novel framework for personalized feedback, competency assessment, and adaptive curriculum design.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether eye-tracking technology, which records where a person looks, could help measure how skilled surgical residents are at their jobs by studying their visual attention patterns during operations. Fifty-seven surgical residents at different training levels watched short video clips of surgical procedures while special cameras tracked exactly where their eyes focused, measuring things like how long they looked at specific areas and how organized their viewing patterns were. The study identified three distinct visual learning styles: experienced residents showed focused, deliberate looking patterns with organized scan paths, junior residents displayed brief but structured viewing, and the least experienced residents showed scattered, exploratory eye movements across the surgical field. These eye-tracking patterns revealed meaningful differences in how residents think about and approach surgery that went beyond simply comparing residents by their year of training. The findings suggest that personalized feedback and training programs could be designed based on each resident's individual visual learning style rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach based on how many years they have been training.

title: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty for fracture: how does a contemporary lateralized prosthesis compare with a Grammont-style implant?
abstract: Reverse shoulder arthroplasty is considered for displaced geriatric proximal humerus fractures (PHFs). This study compared clinical and radiographic outcomes of "Grammont-style" medialized and contemporary lateralized implants, hypothesizing that contemporary implants yield greater range of motion and tuberosity healing.This retrospective single-institution case series reviewed 74 shoulders (74 patients) treated for acute PHFs from 2008-2020. Patients received a medialized reverse shoulder arthroplasty (M-rTSA) (Delta Xtend; n = 31) or lateralized reverse shoulder arthroplasty (L-rTSA) prosthesis (ReUnion RFX; n = 43). Outcomes included visual analog scale pain scores, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores, and range of motion. Tuberosity healing was classified radiographically as anatomic, malunion, nonunion, partial migration, or resorption.The mean follow-up was 34.2 and 19.9 months for the M-rTSA and L-rTSA groups, respectively, with no significant demographic differences. L-rTSA shoulders demonstrated greater external rotation (45° vs. 31°; P = .02). Healing rates of 48% and 86% were observed for M-rTSA and L-rTSA shoulders, respectively. There were no significant differences in forward elevation, complications, or American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons or pain scores. Anatomic tuberosity healing was associated with better rotation and pain scores.Lateralized implants were associated with improved tuberosity healing and external rotation compared to Grammont-style implants for acute PHFs. Tuberosity healing was correlated with better clinical outcomes.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether newer shoulder replacement designs work better than older designs for treating broken upper arm bones in elderly patients. The study looked back at 74 patients who received one of two types of reverse shoulder replacements, which flip the normal ball-and-socket design to help people with certain injuries, comparing a traditional medialized design to a newer lateralized design that positions the ball socket differently. The newer lateralized implants produced better results, including greater ability to rotate the arm outward and much higher healing rates of the broken bone pieces, with 86 percent healing compared to 48 percent in the traditional design group. Patients whose broken bone pieces healed in the correct position experienced better pain relief and improved arm movement, suggesting that the healing of these bone fragments is directly connected to how well patients recover. These findings indicate that the newer lateralized shoulder replacement design may be a better choice for elderly patients with broken upper arm bones, though doctors should continue studying these results to confirm the benefits over time.

title: Intermediate clinical endpoints as surrogates for overall survival after salvage prostatectomy.
abstract: To evaluate biochemical recurrence-free survival (BRFS) and metastasis-free survival (MFS) as potential intermediate clinical endpoints (ICEs) for overall survival (OS) in patients undergoing salvage radical prostatectomy (sRP).Evaluable patients were selected from a retrospective dataset, resulting in a cohort of 879 patients with recurrent, non-metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with sRP at 13 centres. ICE surrogacy was evaluated using a two-stage approach: (i) at the individual-patient level by fitting Clayton copula models and estimating Kendall's τ  ( τ  >0.7 indicating a strong association) and (ii) at the centre level, by fitting weighted linear regression of 5-year OS on 3-year BRFS and MFS.The two-step analysis included 759 patients for BRFS (366 events) and 476 for MFS (137 events), with median follow-up of 37 months (95% confidence interval [CI] 36-42 months) and 34 months (95% CI 31-37 months), respectively. At the individual-patient level, MFS showed a strong association with OS (Kendall's τ  0.85, 95% CI 0.82-0.88), which was not observed for BRFS (Kendall's τ  0.63, 95% CI 0.56-0.69). At the centre level, neither 3-year BRFS (R2 = 0.15; slope = 0.34, P = 0.2) nor 3-year MFS (R2 = 0.21; slope = 0.26, P = 0.14) predicted 5-year OS with sufficient explanatory power. Limitations include the fact that centre-level analysis was based on single-arm associations rather than on treatment-effect surrogacy across arms, and retrospective data collection.The BRFS should not be used as a surrogate endpoint in the sRP setting. MFS requires further validation in future prospective studies to confirm its association with OS. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether two common measures of cancer treatment success could predict overall survival in men who underwent salvage prostatectomy, which is surgery to remove the prostate after cancer returns following radiation therapy. The study included 879 patients with recurring prostate cancer from 13 medical centers and tracked whether biochemical recurrence-free survival (meaning cancer markers don't return in the blood) and metastasis-free survival (meaning cancer doesn't spread to other parts of the body) could serve as reliable predictors of how long patients would live. The results showed that metastasis-free survival had a strong connection to overall survival when looking at individual patients, but biochemical recurrence-free survival did not show this same strong relationship. When researchers analyzed the data at the center level, neither measure was powerful enough to reliably predict five-year survival rates across different hospitals. The researchers concluded that biochemical recurrence-free survival should not be used as a substitute measure for overall survival in this type of surgery, while metastasis-free survival needs further testing in future studies before it can be confidently used as a predictor.

title: Systemic Mastocytosis in Adults: 2026 Update on Diagnosis, Risk Stratification and Management.
abstract: Systemic mastocytosis (SM) results from clonal proliferation of mast cells (MC) in extra-cutaneous organs.The major criterion is the presence of multifocal MC clusters in the bone marrow and/or extracutaneous organs. Minor diagnostic criteria include elevated serum tryptase level, MC CD25/CD2/CD30 expression, and the presence of activating KIT mutations.Establishing SM subtype as per the International Consensus Classification/World Health Organization classification systems is an important first step. Patients either have indolent/smoldering SM (ISM/SSM) or advanced SM, including aggressive SM (ASM), SM with associated myeloid neoplasm (SM-AMN), or mast cell leukemia. Identification of poor-risk mutations (i.e., ASXL1, RUNX1, SRSF2, NRAS) further refines the risk stratification. Several risk models are available to help assign prognosis in SM patients.Treatment goals for ISM patients are primarily directed towards anaphylaxis prevention/symptom control/osteoporosis treatment. Patients with advanced SM frequently need MC cytoreductive therapy to reverse disease-related organ dysfunction. Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKI) (midostaurin, avapritinib) have changed the treatment landscape in SM. While deep biochemical, histological, and molecular responses have been documented with avapritinib treatment, its efficacy as monotherapy against a multimutated AMN disease component in SM-AMN patients remains unclear. Cladribine continues to have a role for MC debulking, whereas interferon-α has a diminishing role in the TKI era. Treatment of SM-AMN primarily targets the AMN component, particularly if an aggressive disease such as acute leukemia is present. Allogeneic stem cell transplant has a role in such patients. Imatinib has a therapeutic role only in the rare patient with an imatinib-sensitive KIT mutation.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Systemic mastocytosis is a serious blood disorder where abnormal mast cells, which are immune system cells, multiply uncontrollably in organs throughout the body and can cause severe symptoms like dangerous allergic reactions and organ damage. Doctors diagnose this condition by looking for clusters of these abnormal cells in bone marrow samples and checking for specific genetic mutations and protein markers in the blood. The disease comes in different types ranging from mild forms that mainly need symptom management to aggressive forms that require strong treatment to prevent organ failure. New medications called tyrosine kinase inhibitors, particularly avapritinib, have significantly improved treatment options by helping shrink the mast cell populations and reverse some organ damage, though older treatments like cladribine and interferon still play a role in certain situations. Patients with the most aggressive forms may need stem cell transplants, and doctors now use genetic testing to identify which patients have the worst outlook so they can plan the most appropriate treatment strategy.

title: A decision-oriented framework for genomic testing across the prostate cancer continuum.
abstract: Genomic testing is now embedded in contemporary prostate cancer care, yet the clinical meaning of different genomic platforms varies substantially by disease state and clinical context. In localized disease, tissue-based genomic classifiers primarily serve prognostic functions by refining risk estimates beyond clinicopathologic variables, whereas in advanced disease, germline and somatic testing identify predictive biomarkers linked to therapy selection. This distinction is clinically consequential because the supporting evidence, endpoints, and implementation challenges differ across assays and across points on the disease continuum. In this review, we position tissue-based assays, germline testing, somatic sequencing, circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), and artificial intelligence-enabled biomarkers within a unified clinical framework spanning localized disease, biochemical recurrence, and metastatic progression. We critically compare commercially available genomic assays with respect to methodology, specimen type, intended use, validation cohorts, and clinically relevant outcomes. We distinguish prognostic classifiers from predictive biomarkers such as homologous recombination repair deficiency and mismatch repair deficiency, and we evaluate emerging approaches, including liquid biopsy, multimodal integration with imaging, and digital pathology-based algorithms. We further address implementation barriers that may limit real-world impact, including reimbursement uncertainty, disparities in access to next-generation sequencing, limited provider familiarity with genomic interpretation, and the need for patient-centered communication and navigation in genomics-informed care. A clinically useful framework for prostate cancer genomics must therefore move beyond cataloging tests and instead clarify when genomic results change management, where evidence remains immature, and how implementation strategies can improve equity and actionability.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Genomic testing, which involves analyzing a person's genes to understand their disease, has become an important part of treating prostate cancer, but the way these tests are used and what they mean changes depending on the stage of the disease. Researchers reviewed different types of genetic tests used across the entire prostate cancer journey, from early localized disease through advanced stages, comparing how each test works, what samples they need, and what results actually matter for patient care. They found that in early-stage prostate cancer, genetic tests mainly help doctors predict which patients are at higher risk, while in advanced cancer, these tests identify specific genetic changes that determine which medicines will work best for each patient. The study highlights that using genomic testing effectively requires not just having the tests available, but also making sure doctors understand how to interpret results, patients can afford access to testing, and healthcare systems can fairly provide these services to all communities. Moving forward, the field needs to focus less on simply listing all available tests and more on clearly explaining when genetic test results will actually change how doctors treat patients and how to overcome barriers that prevent people from getting these potentially life-saving tests.

title: Medical Screening of Adult Psychiatric Patients Presenting to the Emergency Department.
abstract: Medical screening (often termed "medical clearance") is often performed to exclude acute medical conditions in psychiatric emergency department (ED) presentations. This scoping review aims to map and appraise the currently available literature on medical screening of adult (18 years and older) patients with psychiatric complaints in the ED.We searched Medline, PsycInfo, EMBASE, and Web of Science from inception to April 2025, supplemented by citation searching and expert consultation. Eligible studies of any design included adult patients with psychiatric complaints presenting to general EDs and reported on medical screening practices. Key study characteristics were charted from all eligible articles. Original research articles and society statements underwent thematic analysis.Of 9,128 records screened, 145 publications met inclusion criteria, including 62 original research articles, 74 nonoriginal publications, and 9 society recommendations. Among original research articles with primarily retrospective study design (59.7%) on 34,836 patients and 1,149 health care professionals, we identified 8 themes: laboratory testing (38, 62.9%), history taking (22 studies, 35.5%), vital signs (21, 33.9%), physical examination (19, 30.6%), diagnostic imaging (13, 21.0%), medical screening tools (10, 16.1%), electrocardiography (9, 14.5%), and system-level factors (8, 12.9%). Nonoriginal publications were tabulated. Most society recommendations discouraged routine laboratory testing of psychiatric ED presentations and called for collaboration between emergency medicine and psychiatry stakeholders. None of the society recommendations perfectly adhered to either the National Academy of Medicine recommendations for creating trustworthy guidelines or Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation methodology.Medical screening practices can be categorized into 8 distinct themes, with the greatest amount of data available for laboratory testing, history taking, and vital sign assessment. Studies are predominantly retrospective and high-quality prospective assessments of the diagnostic accuracy of medical screening practices are warranted.Copyright © 2026 American College of Emergency Physicians. llm_summary: Researchers examined how emergency departments screen psychiatric patients for hidden medical problems that might be causing their symptoms, since mental health crises can sometimes be triggered by physical illnesses. The team reviewed 145 published studies and recommendations from medical organizations, analyzing information from nearly 35,000 patients and over 1,100 healthcare workers to understand what screening methods doctors actually use. They found that medical screening practices fall into eight main categories, with the most common being blood tests, patient history interviews, vital sign checks like blood pressure and heart rate, physical examinations, imaging scans, specialized screening tools, heart rhythm tests, and hospital-level policies. Most medical organizations recommended against routinely ordering blood tests for all psychiatric patients in the emergency department and called for better teamwork between emergency doctors and psychiatrists. The researchers concluded that while there is good information about laboratory testing and vital signs, more high-quality studies are needed to determine which screening methods actually work best at catching real medical problems in psychiatric patients.

title: The Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program's role in the evolution of quality in metabolic and bariatric surgery.
abstract: The growing prevalence of obesity has driven the widespread adoption of metabolic and bariatric surgery, recognized as the most effective treatment for this population. To improve the quality of care, several countries have established metabolic and bariatric surgery registries to track outcomes, guide performance benchmarks, and advocate for changes and healthcare improvements. In the United States, collaboration between the American College of Surgeons and the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery led to the creation of the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program, which has been instrumental in advancing these goals. Ongoing participation in Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program has been associated with improved surgical outcomes and enhanced patient safety. Its accreditation standards ensure that participating centers uphold high-quality care and support continuous improvement. Moreover, the program has facilitated the development of standardized guidelines and risk-benefit calculators that are now integral to shared decision-making between patients and providers.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery. llm_summary: Obesity has become increasingly common, and surgery has proven to be the most effective treatment for people struggling with severe weight problems. To make sure patients receive the best possible care, the American College of Surgeons and the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery created a program called the Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery Accreditation and Quality Improvement Program, which tracks how well different surgical centers perform. Hospitals and surgical centers that participate in this program have shown better outcomes for their patients, meaning fewer complications and safer procedures overall. The program sets clear standards that all participating centers must follow and helps develop tools like risk calculators that doctors and patients can use together to make informed decisions about surgery. This quality improvement program has become an important way to ensure that people receiving weight loss surgery get consistent, high-quality care across the country.

title: Patterns of Progression and Clinical Outcomes After First Progression in Patients With Primary Plasma Cell Leukemia.
abstract: Primary plasma cell leukemia (pPCL) is a rare and aggressive plasma cell disorder with inferior outcomes compared with multiple myeloma (MM). However, studies describing outcomes after first progression and subsequent lines of therapy remain limited. We retrospectively analyzed 104 patients with pPCL who progressed after first-line therapy treated at one comprehensive cancer center between 2006 and 2024. Clinical characteristics, treatments, time to next treatment (TTNT), and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methods. All pPCL patients received novel agent-based induction. At the time of analysis, 63% had died; median OS was 39 months. High-risk cytogenetics were present in 71%. The median TTNT after first-line therapy was 10 months. Symptomatic progression occurred in 29% of patients and was associated with significantly inferior subsequent OS (13 vs. 34 months) compared with those experiencing asymptomatic biochemical progression. The TTNT progressively shortened with subsequent lines of therapy (3rd line: 6 months; 4th line: 4 months; 5th line: 3 months). Notable exceptions included pPCL patients with t(11;14) treated with anti-BCL-2-based regimens, who achieved a median TTNT of 13 months. Additionally, 24 patients received anti-BCMA CAR T-cell therapy. With a median follow-up of 21 months, their median TTNT was 32 months. pPCL is characterized by frequent disease progression and diminishing response duration with successive therapeutic lines. Symptomatic progression portends particularly poor outcomes. Anti-BCL-2-based therapy in t(11;14) disease and anti-BCMA CAR T-cell therapy appear to provide more durable disease control and represent important advances for the management of progressed pPCL.© 2026 Wiley Periodicals LLC.

llm_summary: Background:  Syphilis, often called "the great masquerader" in medicine because it can imitate many other diseases and is difficult to diagnose correctly, remains a significant health challenge that requires accurate identification methods. Mass spectrometry is a laboratory technique that can identify substances by measuring their mass and chemical properties, and researchers are exploring how this advanced technology might help doctors more reliably detect and diagnose syphilis in kidney patients.

title: Anhidrosis: An underappreciated factor in dermatologic diseases.
abstract: Dissipation of body heat, essential to human life, is largely achieved through sweating. If sweating does not occur normally-as in patients with hypohidrosis (reduced sweating) or anhidrosis (lack of sweating)-the ability to dissipate heat via evaporative mechanisms is overwhelmed. Body temperature may rise, leading to heat-related illness, including heat intolerance, hyperthermia, heat exhaustion, heat stroke, and even death. In patients seen by a dermatologist, anhidrosis may underly and contribute to their symptoms and signs but may be difficult to detect given a limited availability of tools to measure anhidrosis. An association between anhidrosis and skin symptoms including flushing syndromes (eg, facial flushing and erythromelalgia) and widespread skin symptoms (eg, itching, burning, numbness, or tingling, and paresthesias) has recently been described. This review explores the existing dermatologic literature on anhidrosis including clues to the pathophysiology of these disorders, its relationship to skin diseases and symptoms, the tests currently available, and approaches to management. Recognition of an underlying anhidrosis by dermatologists may be important for providing optimal management for patients with heat-related symptoms.Copyright © 2026 American Academy of Dermatology, Inc. llm_summary: Sweating is how our bodies cool down, and when people cannot sweat normally, they face serious health risks like dangerously high body temperature, heat exhaustion, and even death. Dermatologists, who are skin doctors, sometimes see patients with anhidrosis, which means a complete lack of sweating, but they often miss this condition because there are not many good tools available to measure it. Recent research has found that anhidrosis may be connected to several skin problems, including facial flushing and a condition called erythromelalgia where skin becomes red and painful, as well as symptoms like itching, burning, and tingling sensations. This review article gathered information from existing medical studies to help dermatologists understand anhidrosis better, including how it develops, which skin diseases it relates to, what tests can detect it, and how to treat it. Recognizing that a patient has anhidrosis could help skin doctors provide better care for people who experience heat-related symptoms and uncomfortable skin sensations.

title: Vasectomy reversal outcomes and long-term kinetics: a multiinstitutional cohort.
abstract: To compare vasectomy reversal outcomes among surgeons, including long-term success rates.Datasets from eight centers were collated to perform analyses. Some centers maintained prospective databases of outcomes, whereas others performed a retrospective chart review to abstract preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative information.Men undergoing vasectomy reversals for fertility purposes.Descriptive and comparative analyses of the datasets were performed to evaluate differences in outcomes across surgical centers.The primary outcome measures were patency and sperm concentration at 1 year after reversal. Secondary outcomes included comparisons among preoperative patient factors, postoperative patency/concentrations at various timepoints, and changes in sperm kinetics over time. Only variables with at least 10 datapoints were included in the analyses.A total of 4,568 patients were analyzed, with 2,398 having ≥2 semen analyses and 1,222 with at least one test >1 year. Patency rates at 1-year among surgeons ranged from 54%-93% (median of surgeons 82%), with median concentrations of 0-18.5 million/mL (median of surgeons 10.3 million/mL). Although preoperative patient characteristics were relatively similar, nearly every operative and postoperative factor assessed was statistically different among surgeons. Epididymovasostomy rates were linearly correlated with time since vasectomy. Although sperm patency and concentrations demonstrated a general decline over time, outcomes were surgeon-dependent and, counterintuitively, appeared inversely correlated with time since vasectomy (i.e., longer duration since vasectomy may have better patency long-term). In analyzing factors that were able to discriminate outcomes among surgeons, the use of sperm testing at 1 year appeared superior to earlier time points, with no appreciable differences observed using >0, ≥1 million/mL, or ≥5 million/mL sperm concentrations. Patients with tests >1 year had poorer outcomes compared with those without testing >1 year, suggesting that the currently reported findings at >1 year may be overly pessimistic and may overrepresent those with poorer initial results.Patency rates and sperm concentration at 1 year vary widely among surgeons, with median sperm concentration generally declining as time since vasectomy reversal increases. Sperm outcomes at 1 year additionally appear to better discriminate among surgeons compared with other time points and may represent a preferred time point for defining success. Given the inherent limitations of retrospective data, the results likely underestimate true long-term outcomes.Copyright © 2026 American Society for Reproductive Medicine. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Researchers examined vasectomy reversal surgery, which is a procedure to restore fertility in men who previously had vasectomies, to understand how successful different surgeons are at this operation and how long the results last. The study combined data from eight medical centers involving 4,568 men who had vasectomy reversals, tracking their sperm counts and fertility outcomes through semen tests at various time points after surgery. The results showed that success rates varied dramatically among surgeons, with patency rates (meaning the surgical connection was open and working) ranging from 54 percent to 93 percent, and sperm concentrations ranging from zero to 18. 5 million per milliliter depending on the surgeon. Testing at the one-year mark after surgery appeared to be the best time point for measuring success and comparing surgeon outcomes, and surprisingly, men who had waited longer since their original vasectomy sometimes had better long-term results.

title: International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation Scientific Statement on pulmonary antibody-mediated rejection and proposed graft, antibody, and pathology (GAP) definition.
abstract: Antibody-mediated rejection (AMR) is an increasingly recognized form of rejection and cause of graft failure after lung transplantation. AMR has been the focus of extensive research over the past decade. Despite growing awareness and recent advances in our understanding of AMR, outcomes remain dismal with a 2-year survival of only 20%. The International Society for Heart and Lung Transplantation convened a multidisciplinary workgroup of experts in AMR to review the most up-to-date research and clinical experience and to update the 2016 definition. The workgroup was divided into 9 subgroups covering a broad range of topics pertaining to AMR and used the modified Delphi method to synthesize a cohesive summary of the literature. A multidimensional definition was developed to enhance precision by reporting the specific presenting features. This Graft, Antibody, and Pathology (GAP) definition is based on the presence of Graft dysfunction, the presence and characteristics of Antibodies, and Pathological findings. The workgroup emphasized that identifying better treatments for AMR is a critical unmet need and proposed that a more precise definition might allow better management by providing a platform for testing and developing new therapies.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Antibody-mediated rejection, which occurs when a patient's immune system attacks a transplanted lung through proteins called antibodies, is becoming a more common cause of transplant failure with very poor survival rates of only twenty percent at two years. A large group of international lung transplant experts gathered to review all the latest research and clinical experience about this type of rejection and created an updated definition to replace an older one from two thousand sixteen. The experts developed a new framework called the Graft, Antibody, and Pathology definition that looks at three key areas: whether the transplanted lung is working properly, what antibodies are present and how they behave, and what physical changes are visible when tissue samples are examined under a microscope. The researchers believe that having a more precise and detailed definition of antibody-mediated rejection will help doctors better manage patients and create a clearer way to test and develop new treatments for this serious condition. The workgroup emphasized that finding better treatments for this type of rejection remains an urgent and unmet medical need that requires continued research and development of new therapies.

title: Therapeutic Outcomes in VEXAS Syndrome: A Multicenter Comparative Cohort of Allogeneic Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation and Hypomethylating Agents.
abstract: Hypomethylating agents (HMA) and allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (alloHSCT) have both demonstrated remissions in VEXAS; however, comparative data is lacking. We conducted a multicenter, retrospective analysis of 66 patients diagnosed with VEXAS syndrome treated with HMA (n = 35) or alloHSCT (n = 31). Baseline characteristics such as genetics, co-morbidities, and performance status were balanced between the groups, except older age in the HMA group. Median follow-up from therapy initiation was 18 months (95% CI: 11-26), and 14 (21%) deaths were reported (alloHSCT n = 3; HMA n = 11). Among all evaluable patients within the alloHSCT cohort, all patients achieved molecular remission, and a substantial proportion of patients discontinued glucocorticoids (58%). In contrast, HMA therapy was associated with lower but meaningful rates of molecular remission (22%) and glucocorticoid discontinuation (6%). In a real-world setting, HMA therapy was associated with a high discontinuation rate related to toxicity or lack of response. On multivariable analysis adjusted for age and Charlson Comorbidity Index, alloHSCT was associated with improved overall survival (HR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.05-0.81; p = 0.024). This association remained consistent across multiple ancillary sensitivity analyses, including restriction to transplant-eligible patients, patients aged ≤ 75 years, 1:1 matching, and propensity score-based weighted analyses. Although limited by retrospective design, these findings suggest that alloHSCT remains an attractive and potentially curative strategy in selected patients with VEXAS. llm_summary: Researchers examined two different treatment approaches for VEXAS syndrome, a rare blood disorder that causes inflammation and other serious health problems, because doctors needed to know which treatment works better. The study compared 66 patients who received either hypomethylating agents (medicines that change how genes work) or allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (a procedure where healthy blood-forming cells from a donor are placed into a patient's body) and tracked their outcomes over about 18 months. title: Global prevalence and disability burden of brain disorders: Impact of neurological, mental, and substance use disorders.
abstract: Brain disorders-encompassing neurological, mental, and substance use disorders-account for 10 of the top 25 causes of disability worldwide according to the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 study. Despite such an impact, they have not been centrally analyzed in prior GBD studies. This paper synthesizes the latest disability-focused GBD study to quantify the prevalence and disability burden of 35 conditions from 2010 to 2021, a period marking the first decline in global health outcomes in three decades. It further incorporates disability metrics from 2021 to 2023 to contextualize post-pandemic trends. The paper covers the prevalence and disability burden of neurological, mental, and substance use disorders along with COVID-19 using disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) and years lived with disability (YLDs) metrics. From 2010-2021, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and migraine (in neurological disorders), major depressive, anxiety, and eating disorders (in mental disorders), and opioid and drug use disorders (in substance use disorders) showed the greatest increases in age-adjusted prevalence rates across both sexes. In 2021, neurological disorders were the largest contributor to DALYs among brain-disorder categories, while depressive and anxiety disorders ranked as the 2nd and 6th leading causes of global YLDs. Alzheimer's disease/dementias, Parkinson's disease, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), depressive and anxiety disorders, and opioid and drug use disorders showed the largest increases in burden within their respective categories between 2010 and 2021. In both 2021 and 2023, females had higher prevalence rates of overall neurological disorders, headache/migraine, multiple sclerosis, depressive/anxiety disorders, and anorexia nervosa, while males had higher rates of stroke, Parkinson's disease, ASD/ADHD, and substance use disorders. In DALY/YLD metrics, females showed higher rates for anorexia nervosa and multiple sclerosis, and males for ASD, certain neurological disorders, COVID-19, and substance use disorders. In the 2021-2023 extension analysis, disability data showed increases in prevalence and disability of several brain disorders, mostly anxiety disorders, while the COVID-19 disability burden declined markedly by 2023. Further sex-specific disability burden metrics, key insights from each disorder, and limitations/confounds are discussed.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Ltd.. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Brain disorders, which include neurological conditions like Parkinson's disease and Alzheimer's disease, mental health problems like depression and anxiety, and substance use disorders, rank among the top causes of disability worldwide, affecting millions of people and their quality of life. Researchers analyzed global health data from 2010 to 2021 to measure how common these brain disorders are and how much disability they cause, using standard metrics that count both years lost to premature death and years spent living with illness or disability. The study found that conditions like Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, and migraines increased significantly over this period, while depression and anxiety disorders became leading causes of disability globally, with substance use disorders also showing major increases. The research revealed important differences between men and women, with women experiencing higher rates of migraines, multiple sclerosis, depression, and anxiety disorders, while men had higher rates of stroke, Parkinson's disease, autism spectrum disorder, and substance use problems. These findings highlight the urgent need for better prevention and treatment strategies for brain disorders and suggest that future research should continue tracking how these conditions change over time and affect different populations differently.

title: Identification and quantification of Hypocretin-1/Orexin-A 1-14 and 1-16 fragments in immunopurified cerebrospinal fluid using LC-MS: Comparison with radioimmunoassay (RIA) determinations.
abstract: Hypocretin-1/Orexin-A is associated with stabilization of the sleep/wake cycle. Reductions of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) concentrations of orexin-A, as determined by radioimmunoassay (RIA), are considered consistent with the diagnosis of narcolepsy type 1 (NT1). However, measuring full-length orexin-A by other methods such as liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) has proven technically challenging. In this investigation, abundant fragments of orexin-A in CSF were identified and quantified using LC-MS, which allowed assessment of the concordance with clinical RIA measurements.Orexin-A-related peptides were immunopurified using the antibody employed in the RIA from 80 residual CSF samples submitted to our reference laboratory for RIA testing (n = 31, ≤110 pg/mL (low); n = 15, 111-200 pg/mL (intermediate); n = 34, >200 pg/mL (normal)). Enriched peptides then underwent LC-MS/MS analysis, resulting in identification of abundant orexin-A fragments. Following the identification of fragments, quantitative targeted LC-MS measurements were compared to a clinically relevant RIA assay.Full-length orexin-A was not detected in CSF, but two relatively abundant N-terminal orexin-A fragments, comprising amino acids 1-14 and 1-16, were identified by LC-MS/MS. Comparison with RIA yielded Spearman's correlation coefficients (ρ) of 0.91 and 0.94 for the 1-14 and 1-16 fragments, respectively. Additionally, the LC-MS and RIA method were 88% concordant for orexin-A deficient categorizations characteristic of NT1.Quantitative measurement of the identified orexin-A peptide fragments via LC-MS may represent a significant advance in diagnostic capabilities for evaluating central hypersomnolence disorders. These findings also lay the foundation for future studies on the diagnostic utility and clinical relevance of these orexin-A fragments.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a brain chemical called orexin-A, which helps control sleep and wake cycles, because low levels of this chemical in spinal fluid are used to diagnose narcolepsy type 1, a serious sleep disorder. The study team took spinal fluid samples from eighty patients and used two different laboratory methods to measure orexin-A: an older technique called radioimmunoassay and a newer, more precise method called liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. The researchers discovered that full-length orexin-A was not actually present in the spinal fluid, but instead found two smaller fragments of the molecule that were abundant and could be reliably measured. The two measurement methods showed very strong agreement with each other, correctly identifying patients with low orexin-A levels eighty-eight percent of the time, which suggests the newer method could be just as useful as the traditional test for diagnosing sleep disorders. This research opens the door for doctors to use more advanced and precise testing methods to diagnose narcolepsy and other sleep disorders in the future.

title: Distal clavicle autograft: a relatively simple solution for glenoid bone loss at the time of revision reverse arthroplasty.
abstract: Glenoid bone loss is commonly encountered at the time of revision reverse shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA). The ipsilateral distal clavicle has been considered as one possible source of autograft if needed at the time of revision rTSA. The purpose of this study was to determine the outcome of ipsilateral distal clavicle autograft (IDCA) at the time of revision rTSA with particular attention to survival of the glenoid baseplate.Between 2017 and 2023, 20 consecutive revision rTSAs were performed at a single institution using IDCA augmentation of glenoid defects. The mean age at the time of surgery was 74 ± 12 years. Failed prostheses revised included 13 anatomic total shoulder arthroplasties and 7 failed rTSAs. According to the Kocsis classification, pre-operative bone loss was considered stage 2 in 12 shoulders and stage 3 in 8 shoulders. Intraoperatively, 15 patients had central bone defects and 5 patients had combined bone loss using Antuña classification. Clinical assessment was performed pre-operatively and post-operatively for pain, subjective, and objective scores. Radiographic evaluation analyzed the position of the glenoid component as well as radiographic evidence of graft incorporation and loosening. The mean follow-up time was 44 ± 12 months.Mean visual analog scale scores for pain decreased 7 pre-operatively to 1 at most recent follow-up (P < .001). Active elevation and external rotation were improved as well (active elevation = 89° pre-operatively vs. 111° at most recent follow-up [P < .01]; external rotation = 22 pre-operatively degrees vs. 32° at most recent follow-up [P < .01]). Constant scores, American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores, and subjective shoulder values also improved from pre-operatively to most recent (34 points vs. 58 points, P < .001 for Constant scores; 31 points vs. 65 points, P < .001 for American Shoulder and Elbow Surgeons scores; 30% vs. 64% for subjective shoulder values, P < .001). Two revisions were performed for recurrence of infection. One additional shoulder underwent irrigation and débridement with implant retention and one shoulder underwent closed reduction of a dislocation. For the 18 shoulders with no re-revision for infection, IDCA appeared radiographically incorporated, and there was no evidence of glenoid loosening.At mid-term follow-up, IDCA provided a reliable option for moderate glenoid bone loss encountered at the time of revision rTSA. A major benefit of IDCA is availability from the same surgical site of the revision procedure, even if pre-operative assessment underestimated bone loss. These results need to be confirmed in a larger sample size and with longer follow-up.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Glenoid bone loss, which is the wearing away of the shoulder socket, commonly occurs when patients need revision reverse shoulder replacement surgery, meaning they are having a previously implanted artificial shoulder replaced again. Researchers examined twenty patients who underwent this revision surgery between 2017 and 2023, using bone from the patient's own distal clavicle, which is the outer end of the collarbone, to fill in the missing shoulder socket bone. The patients showed significant improvements after surgery, with pain decreasing from a score of 7 to 1, shoulder movement increasing, and overall function scores improving substantially across multiple measures. Among the eighteen patients who did not require another revision surgery for infection, the bone graft appeared to have successfully integrated into the shoulder socket with no signs of the artificial component loosening. While these results are encouraging and show that using a patient's own collarbone bone is a practical solution for moderate bone loss during revision shoulder surgery, the researchers note that larger studies with longer follow-up periods are needed to confirm these findings.

title: Mirrors and prisms: How interprofessional interactions influence medical students' professional identity formation.
abstract: Professional identities impact professional boundaries and hierarchies, influencing how physicians approach collaboration. Despite the growing emphasis on developing students to become effective collaborators, little is known about how other health professionals (OHPs) shape students' professional identity formation (PIF). This study explored how interacting with OHPs during clinical care contributed to medical students' construction of what it means to be a physician.For this constructivist grounded theory study, researchers conducted 20 semi-structured interviews with medical students during clinical clerkships. Students drew rich pictures representing their interactions with OHPs and described these pictures during their interviews. Interviews were iteratively conducted and analysed, enabling the research team to theorize how interacting with OHPs contributed to medical students' PIF.Participants expressed a strong desire to contribute to patient care and described how interprofessional interactions provided opportunities to do so in ways aligned with their current capabilities. These opportunities were often more accessible than the roles and responsibilities of physicians, and participating alongside OHPs fostered participants' sense of their own developing capabilities and belonging on healthcare teams. Interactions with OHPs helped participants to see the expertise of OHPs and the value of collaborating with them in ways that shifted their focus away from becoming independent. Conceptually, participants' interactions with OHPs became both a mirror reflecting their present readiness to meaningfully contribute and a prism through which they could envision their future identities as physicians in new ways.Interprofessional interactions influenced medical students' current and future professional identities, enabling students to see themselves as contributors on health care teams and highlighting collaboration and interdependence as core attributes of the physician profession. These findings highlight opportunities to amplify the impact of interprofessional interactions on the PIF of medical students and the need for research into how OHPs view their roles in these processes.© 2026 Association for the Study of Medical Education and John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how interactions between medical students and other healthcare professionals, such as nurses and physical therapists, shape how students develop their identity as future doctors. The study involved interviewing twenty medical students during their clinical training and asking them to draw pictures representing their experiences working alongside other healthcare professionals, then discussing these drawings in detail. Students reported that working with other healthcare professionals gave them meaningful ways to contribute to patient care that matched their current skill level, which helped them feel like valued members of the healthcare team. The interactions served two important purposes: they acted like a mirror showing students what they were capable of doing right now, and like a prism that helped them imagine new ways of being a doctor in the future, particularly as someone who works collaboratively rather than independently. These findings suggest that healthcare training programs should create more opportunities for medical students to work with other healthcare professionals, since these interactions help students see themselves as team players and understand that good doctors work together with many different types of healthcare workers.

title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor-Related Myositis and Associated Triad Overlap Syndrome.
abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) myositis is a rare but a highly morbid condition, particularly with the ICI myositis triad syndrome of myositis, myocarditis, and myasthenia gravis. We report the clinical characteristics of ICI myositis and all-cause mortality in these patients.We performed a national retrospective cohort study of US veterans treated with an ICI between June 2011 and February 2022. Cases were identified by elevated creatinine kinase (CK) following ICI therapy and/or "myositis" in notes. Chart review determined if candidates had ICI-associated myositis and were subsequently classified as isolated ICI myositis or ICI triad syndrome.Of 29,296 veterans treated with ICIs, 68 (0.2%) ICI-induced myositis cases were identified, including 23 patients with ICI triad syndrome and 45 patients with isolated ICI myositis. Median survival duration for ICI triad syndrome was 2.5 (95% confidence interval [CI] 1.7-18.5) months in comparison to 20.4 (95% CI 6.2-60) months for isolated ICI myositis and 12.6 (95% CI 12.3-12.8) months median survival for patients treated with ICI without myositis. Patients with ICI triad syndrome had 60.0% mortality during the six months following initiation of ICI treatment, in comparison to 30.2% mortality in isolated ICI myositis and 31.5% mortality in patients without myositis. Six months after the first ICI treatment, subsequent mortality trends were similar in the three groups.ICI triad syndrome is associated with higher overall mortality and shortened median survival times during the first six months after initial ICI therapy, whereas isolated ICI myositis is associated with similar mortality outcomes compared to patients treated with ICI who did not develop myositis.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined a serious side effect that can occur when cancer patients receive immune checkpoint inhibitor drugs, which are medications that help the body fight cancer by boosting the immune system. The study looked at nearly thirty thousand veterans who received these cancer drugs between 2011 and 2022, tracking which patients developed myositis, a condition where muscles become inflamed and damaged. They found that sixty-eight patients developed muscle inflammation after treatment, and twenty-three of these patients developed a particularly dangerous combination of three conditions at once: muscle inflammation, heart inflammation, and a nerve disease that weakens muscles. Patients who developed all three conditions together had a much worse outcome, with a median survival time of only two and a half months compared to twenty months for those with muscle inflammation alone. These findings suggest that doctors should watch closely for this dangerous three-condition combination in cancer patients receiving these immune-boosting drugs, since catching and treating it early might improve survival chances.

Pulsed field ablation is a newer technique that uses electrical pulses instead of heat or cold to treat these dangerous heart rhythms, and major medical organizations are now providing guidance on how and when doctors should use this innovative approach.

title: Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: Factors Associated with Multiple Postpartum Blood Pressure Visits.
abstract: Patients with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDPs) are recommended to attend an early postpartum follow-up visit for blood pressure monitoring. Follow-up frequency for patients with HDPs can vary widely, with some patients requiring multiple office visits. We sought to determine factors associated with multiple postpartum blood pressure visits among patients with HDPs.We retrospectively identified patients with HDPs who delivered at our maternity center in 2019 and compared factors between patients who attended a single blood pressure follow-up appointment without requiring further clinical evaluation for hypertension and patients who required multiple postpartum clinical evaluations for persistent hypertension. Univariate logistic regression models were used to identify factors associated with increased odds of having multiple clinically indicated postpartum visits for blood pressure monitoring.We identified 328 patients with HDPs, of whom 260 (79.3%) attended an initial postpartum blood pressure follow-up appointment and were included in further analyses. Of the 260 patients, 70 (26.9%) had multiple blood pressure visits. Factors associated with multiple blood pressure visits included delivery between 34 and less than 37 weeks of gestation (odds ratio [OR], 3.62; 95% CI, 1.07-12.30), systolic blood pressure before discharge of 140 mm Hg or higher (OR, 5.02; 95% CI, 2.57-9.82), and discharge with blood pressure medication (OR, 3.42; 95% CI, 1.82-6.41).Patients with HDPs who deliver preterm, have persistent hypertension before discharge, or are discharged with antihypertensive medication require continued close postpartum observation and continuity of care.· Postpartum follow-up care for patients with HDPs should be tailored to the patient.. · Preterm delivery, persistence of hypertensive blood pressure at discharge, and discharge with antihypertensive medication are associated with multiple postpartum ambulatory office visits.. · High-risk patients should be diligently monitored with postpartum continuity of care..Thieme. llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who developed high blood pressure during pregnancy, a serious condition that requires careful monitoring after delivery to prevent complications. The study looked back at medical records from 2019 to compare patients who needed only one follow-up blood pressure check after giving birth with those who needed multiple visits because their high blood pressure persisted. Among the 260 patients included in the analysis, about 27 percent required multiple postpartum visits, and the researchers found that three factors predicted who would need extra monitoring: delivering the baby before 37 weeks of pregnancy, having a systolic blood pressure reading of 140 or higher at hospital discharge, and going home while taking blood pressure medication. These findings suggest that doctors should pay special attention to pregnant patients with high blood pressure who fall into these higher-risk categories and ensure they receive consistent follow-up care after delivery. Healthcare providers should customize their postpartum monitoring plans based on each patient's individual risk factors rather than using a one-size-fits-all approach.

title: Syndromes Aassociated with Lipomatous Tumors (SALT): A comprehensive review.
abstract: Lipomas are among the most common specimens encountered in surgical pathology. Beyond distinguishing a lipoma from an atypical lipomatous tumor or well-differentiated liposarcoma (ALT/WDLS), there are important clinical considerations to keep in mind, as lipomas and lipomatosis may occur in association with various syndromes. These syndromes can be inherited or sporadic, and some are linked to an increased risk of other malignancies. Moreover, several are associated with systemic findings that carry significant morbidity and mortality. Careful attention to specific clinicopathologic features-together with molecular testing when indicated-can facilitate early recognition of these syndromes, which is essential for appropriate counseling and long-term surveillance. Despite numerous case reports and isolated studies, a comprehensive synthesis of these syndromes remains lacking. In this review, we aim to summarize the Syndromes Associated with Lipomatous Tumors (SALT) and highlight key clinicopathologic features relevant to diagnosis and management. We also hope that this overview will stimulate further research by providing a succinct framework for exploring potential biologic networks underlying the origin and development of these common neoplasms.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Lipomas, which are common fatty tumors found in the body, can sometimes be a sign of larger health syndromes that run in families or occur randomly and may increase the risk of other cancers. This review brings together information about various syndromes linked to lipomas and fatty tissue overgrowth, highlighting the specific features doctors should look for when examining tissue samples under a microscope. The researchers emphasize that careful attention to how these tumors appear, combined with genetic testing when needed, can help doctors recognize these syndromes early so they can provide proper patient counseling and plan appropriate long-term monitoring. Understanding these syndromes is important because some are associated with serious health problems beyond just the fatty tumors themselves, and some increase the likelihood of developing other types of cancer. By organizing what is known about these syndromes into one comprehensive guide, the authors hope to help doctors better diagnose and manage patients while also encouraging scientists to investigate the underlying biological reasons why these common tumors develop in people with these conditions.

title: Risk stratification in short QT syndrome: Findings from a pooled analysis.
abstract: In long QT syndrome, longer QT intervals indicate increased arrhythmic risk, and a rate-corrected QT interval (QTc) of ≥500 ms denotes high risk. Establishing similar associations in short QT syndrome (SQTS) remains elusive.This study aimed to demonstrate that shorter QT intervals denote a higher risk of malignant arrhythmias in SQTS and to define the "high-risk" QTc value in SQTS.Pooled analysis of patients treated in our institutions or those reported in the literature revealed 162 patients with SQTS and known symptomatic status; 57 of them (35.2%) had arrhythmic symptoms (sudden death, cardiac arrest, or malignant syncope).There was a significant inverse association between the QTc and arrhythmic symptoms (with a median QTc of 315.0 ms [interquartile range 300.5-338.0] among symptomatic patients vs 330.0 ms [interquartile range 312.5-355.0] among asymptomatic patients; P = .0023). Receiver operator characteristics analysis showed that shorter QTc values were associated with a higher risk (area under the curve 0.64 ± 0.04; P = .0024). When patients were grouped by QTc range, most of those with a QTc of ≤320 ms had malignant arrhythmic symptoms, whereas the reverse was true for those with a QTc of ≥320 ms. Male patients were overrepresented in the SQTS cohort and more so in the subgroup with malignant symptoms.This pooled analysis of patients with SQTS demonstrates that, among patients with congenital SQTS, a shorter QTc is associated with a higher risk of malignant ventricular arrhythmias. A QTc shorter than 320 ms correlates with a higher arrhythmic risk. Men seem to be at higher risk.Copyright © 2026 Heart Rhythm Society. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined a group of patients with short QT syndrome, a rare heart condition where the electrical activity of the heart happens faster than normal, to figure out which patients are at highest risk for dangerous heart rhythms and sudden death. They combined information from 162 patients treated at their hospitals or reported in medical literature, looking at the relationship between how fast each patient's heart electrical activity occurred and whether they experienced life-threatening symptoms like cardiac arrest or fainting spells. The study found that patients with the shortest electrical activity measurements, specifically those with a corrected QT interval shorter than 320 milliseconds, were much more likely to have experienced dangerous heart problems compared to those with longer measurements. The results showed that in short QT syndrome, the opposite pattern exists compared to long QT syndrome, where shorter measurements mean higher risk rather than longer ones. Men made up most of the study group and were even more overrepresented among the patients who had experienced dangerous symptoms, suggesting they may face greater risk from this condition.

title: Temporary mechanical circulatory support in left ventricular assist device candidates with right ventricular dysfunction: Acuity without long-term futility.
abstract: Temporary mechanical circulatory support (tMCS) is increasingly used as a bridge to durable left ventricular assist device (LVAD) implantation in patients with advanced heart failure, particularly those with right ventricular dysfunction (RVD). RVD at the time of LVAD implantation predicts early morbidity and mortality, and preoperative tMCS has been associated with inferior survival in registry analyses. However, whether tMCS independently contributes to long-term risk or simply identifies high-acuity patients remains unclear.We conducted a retrospective, multicenter cohort study of 201 adult patients with objectively defined RVD undergoing HeartMate 3 implantation between 2018 and 2022. RVD was confirmed by echocardiography (TAPSE <16 mm and/or qualitative RV dysfunction) and invasive hemodynamics (CVP/PCWP >0.54 and/or PAPi <2.0 with cardiac index <2.2L/min/m²). Patients were stratified by preoperative tMCS use. Outcomes included early postoperative morbidity, survival at 1 to 3 years, and conditional survival after 30-, 90-, and 180-days.tMCS patients had higher INTERMACS and EUROMACS-RHF scores, more severe hemodynamic compromise, and greater ventilatory support. They experienced increased early morbidity, including prolonged ICU stay, mechanical ventilation, and higher RVAD utilization. One- and 2-year survival was lower in tMCS patients, but 3-year survival and conditional survival beyond 30 to 180 days were similar between groups. Proportional hazards analysis showed that tMCS was independently associated with earlier but not longer-term mortality.In LVAD recipients with defined RVD, preoperative tMCS identifies patients at heightened early perioperative risk but does not confer durable mortality risk among conditional survivors. These findings underscore the importance of separating early procedural hazard from durable prognosis and caution against interpreting tMCS use as evidence of LVAD futility.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether temporary mechanical heart pumps used before permanent heart device implantation actually harm long-term survival in patients with weakened right heart chambers. The study followed 201 patients with right heart dysfunction who received permanent HeartMate 3 devices between 2018 and 2022, comparing those who had temporary support beforehand to those who did not. Patients who received temporary support had more severe heart problems initially and experienced more complications in the hospital, including longer stays in intensive care and greater need for additional mechanical support. However, when researchers looked at survival rates beyond the first few months, patients in both groups had similar chances of living one, two, and three years after their device implantation. These findings suggest that temporary mechanical support identifies patients who are sicker at the time of surgery but does not doom them to worse long-term outcomes, meaning doctors should not assume that needing temporary support means a permanent heart device will not help.

title: The Great Auricular Point: A Landmark for Safe Sternocleidomastoid Myotomy in Selective Cervical Denervation for Cervical Dystonia.
abstract: Cervical dystonia is the most common focal dystonia, characterized by involuntary muscle contractions leading to abnormal postures and significant discomfort. Although neuromuscular blockade with botulinum toxin and other agents is the primary treatment, selective cervical denervation, which includes sternocleidomastoid (SCM) and posterior cervical muscle denervation, is a surgical option for refractory cases. The aim of this study was to evaluate the great auricular point (GAP) as a reliable intraoperative landmark for selective cervical denervation, optimizing spinal accessory nerve (SAN) preservation during SCM myotomy/denervation.A review of anatomic studies and cadaveric dissections was conducted to assess the GAP's role in guiding safe SCM myotomy and minimizing SAN injury. The anatomic relationship between the GAP, SAN, and great auricular nerve was evaluated for consistency. Subsequently, this technique, including denervation of the accessory nerve branches to SCM, was applied clinically in 5 patients.We report a modification of selective cervical denervation using the GAP technique during SCM myotomy and selective denervation. The GAP was consistently located inferior to the SAN exit site at the posterior SCM border. Shoulder motion and scapular stability were maintained in all 5 patients. The GAP provided a stable reference point for SCM myotomy, effectively preserving the SAN's trapezius branch and enhancing surgical precision.The GAP serves as a reliable intraoperative landmark for selective cervical denervation, facilitating safe SCM myotomy and minimizing iatrogenic SAN injury. In addition, this technique may minimize revisions by providing enhanced visibility and precision during SCM myotomy. Further clinical validation is warranted to confirm its broader efficacy in neurosurgical practice.Copyright © Congress of Neurological Surgeons 2025. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Cervical dystonia is a condition where neck muscles involuntarily contract and cause abnormal postures and pain, and while botulinum toxin injections are the main treatment, surgery is sometimes needed for patients who do not respond to these injections. Researchers reviewed anatomical studies and performed dissections on cadavers to test whether a specific landmark called the great auricular point, located on the neck near the ear, could safely guide surgeons during neck muscle surgery while protecting an important nerve that controls shoulder movement. They found that the great auricular point was consistently positioned below where the spinal accessory nerve exits the muscle, making it a reliable guide for surgeons to follow during the procedure. When surgeons used this landmark technique on five patients, all of them maintained normal shoulder movement and stability after surgery, showing that the technique successfully protected the nerve that controls these movements. The researchers conclude that using the great auricular point as a surgical landmark improves precision and safety during neck muscle surgery for cervical dystonia, though more patients need to be treated with this technique to confirm it works well across a wider population.

title: Efficacy of Topical Timolol in Chronic Unhealed Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BackgroundTopical timolol appears to provide a curative effect in managing chronic ulcers. However, the pooled evidence of its effect hasn't been established yet. This is the first Meta-analysis to evaluate and assess the efficacy of topical timolol in accelerating wound healing in patients with chronic refractory ulcers.MethodsWe comprehensively searched different electronic databases; PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Cochrane library and ClinicalTrials.gov from their inception to November 2024. The search was conducted without imposing any restrictions on publication date or study design. The ROB-II tool was used to assess the quality of included RCTs. NIH tools were used to evaluate the quality of included cohort and single arm studies. Risk ratios (RR) and mean differences (MD), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), were used as effect estimates.ResultsSix studies were included in this systematic review, comprising two single-arm studies and four double-arm studies (3 RCTs and 1 cohort study). Data from the four double-arm studies on venous ulcers were pooled for meta-analysis. The results showed that topical timolol significantly reduced ulcer area compared to control at 2 weeks (-23.63%; 95% CI: -29.26 to -18.00; p < 0.00001), 4 weeks (-41.40%; 95% CI: -49.57 to -33.23; p < 0.00001), and 12 weeks (-23.38%; 95% CI: -39.43 to -7.33; p = 0.004). Complete ulcer healing was observed at 4 weeks (RR: 12.00; 95% CI: 1.68 to 85.84; p = 0.01) and 12 weeks (RR: 3.79; 95% CI: 0.44 to 32.54; p = 0.22).ConclusionTopical timolol has the potential to promote healing in chronic unhealed ulcers. This meta-analysis, focusing on chronic venous ulcers, consistently showed favorable results across different time points. However, the small sample sizes, lack of blinding, and inclusion of only four studies limit the generalizability of the findings.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a common blood pressure medication called timolol, when applied directly to the skin, could help heal chronic wounds that do not improve on their own. The team searched medical databases for all available studies comparing timolol treatment to standard care and combined the results from four high-quality studies involving patients with long-lasting leg ulcers caused by poor blood circulation. The findings showed that timolol significantly reduced the size of ulcers at two weeks, four weeks, and twelve weeks compared to regular treatment, with some patients experiencing complete healing by four weeks. These results suggest that topical timolol could become a helpful new treatment option for people suffering from stubborn wounds that resist conventional healing methods. However, the researchers noted that their conclusions are limited by the small number of patients studied and the lack of proper blinding, meaning both patients and doctors knew who received timolol, which could influence the results.

title: Case series exploring hormonal sensitivity in prostate cancer patients harboring the germline African-ancestry HOXB13 X285K variant.
abstract: Recently, a germline HOXB13 variant, X285K was identified as a risk factor for prostate cancer in men of African ancestry. While this variant is likely associated with more aggressive prostate cancer, there has not yet been an in-depth clinical description of individual patients carrying this variant and their response to systemic therapies.We studied six cases of germline X285K carriers with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer to characterize their hormonal sensitivity or resistance.Longitudinal outcome analysis indicates that patients carrying X285K generally show favorable responses to therapies targeting the androgen receptor (AR), a finding that requires confirmation.© 2025.
