title: Interventions for Increasing Colorectal Cancer Screening Uptake: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Colorectal cancer screening reduces mortality, yet uptake remains suboptimal. Various interventions aim to improve screening rates, but their comparative effectiveness is unclear. We aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of colorectal cancer screening uptake interventions using a systematic review and network meta-analysis.We analyzed data from 76 randomized clinical trials across 8 intervention strategies: patient navigation, mailed fecal immunochemical testing (FIT) outreach, educational multimedia, reminder only, choice-based outreach, colonoscopy outreach, multistep, and usual care. Network meta-analysis compared interventions using risk ratios (RRs) and 95% CIs. P scores and rankograms assessed intervention rankings. Risk of bias was assessed, and certainty of evidence was graded using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation framework.Patient navigation (RR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.23-2.02; P score .81) and mailed FIT outreach (RR, 1.36; 95% CI, 1.07-1.74; P score = .79) were the most effective strategies, significantly outperforming usual care. Educational multimedia (RR, 1.27; 95% CI, 0.91-1.78) and reminder-only interventions (RR, 1.24; 95% CI, 0.98-1.57) showed modest effects. Choice-based outreach and colonoscopy outreach were not significantly more effective than usual care. Mailed FIT outreach was superior to colonoscopy outreach (RR, 1.35; 95% CI, 1.11-1.63), and patient navigation outperformed reminder-only interventions (RR, 1.48; 95% CI, 1.14-1.94). In low baseline uptake settings (<30%), mailed FIT outreach was most effective (RR, 3.12; 95% CI, 1.70-5.71), and educational multimedia performed best in higher uptake populations (≥30%) and in recent studies (2021-2024). The majority of studies were at low risk of bias and the certainty of evidence mostly ranged from moderate to low.Patient navigation and mailed FIT outreach are the most effective strategies for increasing colorectal cancer screening uptake, particularly in low baseline uptake populations. Educational multimedia has shown promise in recent years and high baseline uptake settings, offering a scalable alternative.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Colorectal cancer screening saves lives by catching the disease early, but many people do not get screened, so researchers wanted to find out which methods work best to encourage people to participate. The team reviewed 76 different research studies that tested eight different approaches to boost screening rates, including having someone help guide patients through the process, mailing home test kits, showing educational videos, sending reminders, and offering choices about which screening method to use. Patient navigation, which means having someone personally help guide a patient through screening, and mailing home test kits were found to be the most effective strategies, increasing screening rates by about 36 to 58 percent compared to standard care. In areas where very few people currently get screened, mailing home test kits worked especially well and was much more effective than offering colonoscopy appointments, while educational videos showed the most promise in recent years and in places where screening rates were already higher. The researchers concluded that patient navigation and mailed test kits are the best options for getting more people screened, though they noted that most studies had some limitations in how certain we can be about these results.

title: Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty in Patients Who Have Morbid Obesity: A Propensity-Weighted Analysis of Dual Mobility and Standard Fixed-Bearing Implants.
abstract: Dual mobility (DM) bearings in total hip arthroplasty (THA) are designed to offer enhanced stability compared to traditional fixed-bearing constructs. However, the stability and durability of DM implants in the setting of morbid obesity remain underexplored. This study aimed to compare outcomes of DM and fixed-bearing constructs among morbidly obese patients following primary THA.We retrospectively reviewed patients who had a body mass index (BMI) greater than 40 and underwent primary THA between 2005 and 2022 using an institutional total joint registry. Those who had less than two years of follow-up and fixed-bearing head sizes less than 36 mm were excluded. There were 69 patients who received DM and 943 who received fixed-bearing implants, achieving a mean follow-up of 6.0 years (range, 2.0 to 17.2). The DM patients were older (mean age 63.0 versus 60.8 years, P = 0.032), more commonly women (73.9 versus 43.6%, P < 0.001), had higher BMI (mean 45.5 versus 44.5, P = 0.019), and more frequently underwent posterior approach THA (91.3 versus 59.9%, P < 0.001). Using propensity weighting to adjust for age, sex, BMI, surgical approach, surgical indication, spine disease, and spine surgery, Kaplan-Meier analyses assessed survivorship free from instability, revision, reoperation, and nonoperative complication.Rates of instability were low in both DM and fixed-bearing groups (1.4 versus 0.6%). There were no revisions following DM THA, whereas 43 fixed-bearing constructs required revision (0 versus 4.6%, P = 0.070), including 5 (0.5%) for instability. Reoperation (1.4 versus 7.1%; P = 0.070) and nonoperative complication (5.8 versus 5.5%; P = 0.921) rates were similar. Propensity-weighted 5-year survivorship free from instability, revision, reoperation, and nonoperative complication was 98.6, 100.0, 98.5, and 94.2% for DM and 99.4, 96.8, 94.1, and 92.3% for fixed-bearing implants.In morbidly obese patients, DM implants demonstrated excellent 5-year survivorship with outcomes comparable or slightly superior to fixed-bearing constructs. These findings suggest DM implants may provide stability without increasing complication rates in this high-risk population.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a newer type of hip replacement implant called dual mobility, which has a special ball-and-socket design meant to prevent the hip from popping out of place, works better than traditional hip implants in very obese patients with a body mass index greater than 40. The study looked back at medical records from 2005 to 2022 and compared 69 patients who received the dual mobility implant with 943 patients who received standard implants, following them for an average of six years. Both groups had very low rates of hip dislocation, or the ball slipping out of the socket, but the dual mobility group had no revisions meaning no patients needed a second surgery to replace their implant while 43 patients in the standard implant group did need revision surgery. After five years, the dual mobility implants showed excellent results with 100 percent of patients avoiding the need for revision surgery compared to about 97 percent in the standard implant group. These findings suggest that dual mobility implants may be a good choice for very obese patients undergoing hip replacement because they provide stability without causing more complications than traditional implants.

title: Updated Global Consensus Recommendations for Risk Stratification, Treatment Initiation, and Response Monitoring in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) have increased in prevalence alongside the global epidemics of obesity and type 2 diabetes and now represent one of the leading causes of chronic liver disease. Patients with MASLD and significant fibrosis (≥F2) are at increased risk for adverse outcomes. With advances in noninvasive tests (NITs) and the recent approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for noncirrhotic MASH with F2-F3 fibrosis, we provide updated consensus guidance on standardized risk stratification, treatment initiation, and response monitoring.A structured Delphi process was conducted following a systematic updated literature review (January 2025-November 2025), covering the period since publication of the initial consensus recommendations, and included iterative anonymous voting among 40 international experts representing hepatology, gastroenterology, endocrinology, internal medicine, and primary care. Consensus was predefined as ≥70% agreement.Forty-two statements were developed; 86% achieved consensus in the first round, and all remaining statements reached consensus after refinement and the second round. The panel endorsed a sequential risk-stratification strategy beginning with Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4) as the first-line assessment, followed by vibration-controlled transient elastography or Enhanced Liver Fibrosis (ELF) testing for secondary stratification. Treatment consideration with resmetirom or semaglutide was supported for noncirrhotic MASLD with liver stiffness measurement values of 10 to 20 kPa or ELF values of 9.2 to 11.3, after exclusion of cirrhosis. Upfront combination therapy with both drugs was not recommended. Selection of pharmacologic therapy was to be determined through shared decision-making between patient and provider and individualized according to the patient's cardiometabolic profile. Treatment response at 1 year was defined as a ≥30% reduction in liver stiffness or a ≥0.5-point reduction in ELF.This updated international consensus provides practical algorithms that integrate most commonly used noninvasive testing with recently approved pharmacologic therapies for MASLD, addressing current variability in clinical practice and supporting standardized implementation of risk-based care.Copyright © 2026 American Gastroenterological Association Institute. llm_summary: Fatty liver disease linked to metabolic problems like obesity and diabetes has become one of the most common causes of chronic liver damage worldwide, making it urgent to develop better ways to identify and treat patients at highest risk. An international team of forty medical experts from various specialties used a structured voting process to review the latest scientific evidence and create updated guidelines for identifying which patients need treatment, deciding when to start medications, and measuring whether those medications are working. The experts recommended a step-by-step approach starting with a simple blood test called the Fibrosis-4 Index to screen patients, followed by more detailed imaging or blood tests if needed to confirm how much liver scarring is present. For patients with moderate liver scarring but no cirrhosis, the panel supported using two newly approved medications called resmetirom or semaglutide, chosen based on each patient's individual health needs rather than using both drugs together. These updated recommendations provide doctors with clear, practical steps to standardize how they evaluate and treat fatty liver disease, helping ensure that patients receive consistent, evidence-based care across different healthcare settings.

title: Contemporary Total Hip Arthroplasty for Sequelae of Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis: 15-Year Outcomes of 165 Cases.
abstract: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (SCFE) is a pediatric hip disorder whose sequelae may require total hip arthroplasty (THA) at a young age. The outcomes of contemporary THA in this population need to be defined further. We aimed to evaluate survivorship, complications, radiographic results, and clinical outcomes in this population.We identified 165 THAs performed for sequelae of SCFE between 2000 and 2022. The mean age at THA was 45 years, 71% were men, and they had a mean body mass index of 33. There were 133 hips (81%) with prior surgical treatment, most commonly in situ pinning (58%). Most THA constructs used cementless fixation (96%). Ceramic-on-highly cross-linked polyethylene was the most common bearing surface (47%). The mean follow-up was nine years (range, two to 21).The 15-years survivorships free of aseptic revision, any revision, any reoperation, and any complication were 98, 98, 96, and 89%, respectively. There were three revisions performed for aseptic loosening, liner dissociation, and periprosthetic joint infection. Of 12 complications, 11 occurred within 30 days of THA. In unrevised THA, there was no evidence of loosening at final follow-up. The mean Harris Hip Score improved from 57.1 preoperatively to 89.2 at 10 years (P < 0.001).In the largest reported series on this topic to our knowledge, contemporary THA for sequelae of SCFE demonstrated excellent 15-years survivorship free of revision and reoperation, along with clinical improvements in this unique population.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Slipped capital femoral epiphysis is a childhood hip condition where the thighbone slips out of place, and many patients eventually need hip replacement surgery as adults, making it important to understand how well these replacements work over time. Researchers studied 165 hip replacement surgeries performed on patients with this condition between 2000 and 2022, tracking their outcomes for an average of nine years to see how many replacements lasted without needing revision surgery or experiencing problems. The results showed that 15 years after surgery, 98 percent of the hip replacements did not need to be replaced due to loosening or failure, and patients reported significant improvement in pain and function, with their hip scores improving from 57 before surgery to 89 ten years later. These findings suggest that modern hip replacement surgery is a very effective treatment for adults dealing with the long-term effects of this childhood hip condition, offering them excellent chances of success and improved quality of life. While this is the largest study of its kind on this topic, future research could help identify which patients might benefit most from this surgery and whether any specific surgical techniques produce even better results.

title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome Clinical Care Gaps and the Potential of Future Therapeutics Based on Peripheral Visceral Afferent Modulation.
abstract: Current management of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is focused on bowel dysfunction or central neuromodulators. The aims of this review were to: appraise unmet needs in IBS treatment; review the physiology of visceral afferent functions and specifically receptors in the dorsal root ganglion (DRG) cell bodies of the first order neurones; and summarize evidence of efficacy of pharmacological approaches directed at receptors expressed by DRGs based on rodent models of visceral hypersensitivity and randomized controlled trials in IBS. A literature search was done using terms identified in the aims section. The greatest need in IBS is safe treatment of pain. Physiological and noxious stimuli are conducted to the brain through vagal and pelvic parasympathetic pathways, and noxious stimuli through visceral afferents and spinal cord. Peripheral visceral afferents, with cell bodies in DRG, have receptors targeted pharmacologically to relieve pain (or surrogates) in rodent IBS models of visceral hypersensitivity. Advances in understanding mechanisms of visceral hypersensitivity lead to consideration of targeting receptors on the DRG. Those receptors on DRGs are also expressed in the central nervous system and include α-2 adrenergic, somatostatin-SS2, 5-HT3, cannabinoid, α4β2 and α6β2 nicotininc cholinergic, calcitonin gene-related peptide, κ-opioid and glucagon-like peptide 1 receptors and acid-gated ion channels. Evidence from predominantly pre-clinical and human studies supporting these peripheral targets is summarized, and provides the rationale to develop novel, peripherally restricted pharmaceuticals to reduce visceral pain in IBS. Novel neuromodulators restricted to peripheral actions and targeting DRG receptors would constitute a novel alternative to central neuromodulators for IBS pain, in addition to potential effects on colonic transit or secretion.Copyright © 2026 American Gastroenterological Association Institute. llm_summary: Irritable bowel syndrome, a common digestive disorder that causes stomach pain and irregular bowel movements, is difficult to treat effectively because current medications either focus on fixing bowel problems or work on the brain rather than addressing the root cause of pain. Researchers reviewed scientific studies to understand how pain signals travel from the gut to the brain through special nerve pathways and identified specific receptor sites, which are like locks on nerve cells that medications can target, located in clusters of nerve cells called dorsal root ganglia. The review found that many different types of receptors on these nerve clusters could potentially be blocked or activated by new medications to reduce gut pain, including receptors for substances like serotonin, cannabinoids, and opioids that already exist in the body. Developing new drugs that work only on these peripheral nerve targets rather than affecting the entire brain and nervous system could offer patients a safer way to manage irritable bowel syndrome pain without the side effects associated with current brain-based treatments. The next step is to create and test new medications designed specifically to target these peripheral nerve receptors in actual patients with irritable bowel syndrome to confirm that this approach is both safe and effective.

title: Metabolic exhaustion and immune ageing in rheumatoid arthritis.
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) disproportionately affects adults over 50 years of age, highlighting how age-related immune remodelling undermines tolerance and promotes autoreactivity. In later adulthood, immune cells progressively lose metabolic resilience because of impaired nutrient sensing, reduced metabolic flexibility and disrupted anabolic-catabolic balance. In RA, these vulnerabilities are compounded by mitochondrial insufficiency across innate and adaptive immune lineages, creating a state of nutrient deprivation characterized by NAD⁺ and ATP scarcity and diversion of carbon away from oxidative phosphorylation. Mechanistic studies identify this bioenergetic fragility as a core defect that limits cellular longevity and promotes inflammatory, non-apoptotic death pathways, including pyroptosis and PANoptosis. The hypoxic, nutrient-restricted synovial environment adds pressure that exceeds the diminished metabolic adaptability of aged immune cells. In RA T cells, accelerated mitochondrial injury initiates maladaptive stress responses, disrupts mitochondria-lysosome-endoplasmic reticulum communication and induces gasdermin D-dependent pore formation and inflammatory lysis. Synovial MerTK⁺ reparative macrophages undergo a parallel metabolic crisis, whereby autocrine C1q sensing activates mitochondrial SARM1, causing NAD⁺ degradation, ATP depletion and PANoptotic cell death. Together, these findings position ageing-associated metabolic exhaustion and organelle disintegration as unifying mechanisms that convert immune cells into tissue-damaging effectors and explain the heightened susceptibility to RA in older adults.© 2026. llm_summary: Rheumatoid arthritis, a disease where the immune system attacks the body's own joints, becomes much more common in people over 50 years old because aging changes how the immune system works and makes it more likely to attack the body's own tissues. Researchers examined how immune cells in people with rheumatoid arthritis lose their ability to produce energy efficiently due to problems with mitochondria, which are the power plants inside cells that create the fuel cells need to function. The study found that this energy shortage causes immune cells to die in harmful ways that trigger inflammation rather than dying peacefully, and this problem gets worse in the inflamed environment of damaged joints where oxygen and nutrients are scarce. These findings suggest that the combination of aging and metabolic exhaustion, or the body's inability to maintain proper energy production, transforms immune cells into tissue-damaging agents that explain why older adults are more vulnerable to developing rheumatoid arthritis. Future treatments might focus on restoring the energy-producing ability of immune cells or preventing the harmful death pathways that occur when cells run out of fuel, which could offer new ways to help older patients with this disease.

title: Advances in the treatment of eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
abstract: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) is a small-vessel vasculitis associated with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies and characterized by blood and tissue eosinophilia, severe respiratory manifestations, and multiorgan involvement. The management of newly diagnosed EGPA still relies on therapeutic strategies that were initially validated for other forms of anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated vasculitis, including microscopic polyangiitis and granulomatosis with polyangiitis. Whereas the long-term prognosis of microscopic polyangiitis and granulomatosis with polyangiitis depends primarily on controlling initial organ involvement and preventing relapses, EGPA is distinguished by chronic involvement of both upper and lower respiratory airways, which often necessitates prolonged glucocorticoid therapy. Data from clinical trials suggest that targeting the IL-5 pathway with mepolizumab or benralizumab can effectively control persistent respiratory symptoms and reduce the need for glucocorticoids, yet the role of these agents in the management of EGPA at the time of diagnosis and in the long term remains to be defined. Emerging retrospective data on therapies targeting other type 2 cytokines (such as IL-4, IL-13 and thymic stromal lymphopoietin) suggest potential benefits for relapsing respiratory symptoms; however, prospective evidence remains limited and safety has yet to be established. This Review discusses the role of these new targeted therapies in the management of EGPA, alongside historical treatments.© 2026. Springer Nature Limited.

llm_summary: Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis is a rare disease where the immune system attacks blood vessels and causes high levels of infection-fighting cells called eosinophils to build up in the blood and organs, leading to serious breathing problems and damage to multiple body systems. Currently, doctors treat this disease using the same strong medications that were originally developed for other similar vasculitis conditions, but these treatments often require patients to take steroids for long periods because the disease keeps affecting the lungs and airways. Recent clinical trials have shown that newer medicines targeting a specific immune pathway called IL-5 can help control breathing symptoms and reduce how much steroid medication patients need to take. Other experimental treatments that target different parts of the immune system show promise in early studies for helping patients whose respiratory symptoms keep coming back, but doctors still need more research to confirm these benefits and make sure these drugs are safe. The main challenge ahead is figuring out exactly when and how to use these newer targeted medicines in treating newly diagnosed patients and managing the disease over many years.

title: Vascular Abnormalities in Athletes: State-of-the-Art Multimodality Imaging.
abstract: Vascular abnormalities in athletes, although less common than musculoskeletal injuries, present a significant diagnostic challenge due to overlapping manifestations. These conditions range from subtle exertional discomfort to potentially limb-threatening ischemia and life-threatening complications such as pulmonary embolism or sudden cardiac death. In this comprehensive review, the authors highlight the spectrum of vascular abnormalities encountered in athletes, emphasizing the pivotal role of multimodality imaging, including US, CT angiography, MR angiography, and conventional angiography in their accurate diagnosis and effective management. They discuss upper extremity conditions such as Paget-Schroetter syndrome, quadrilateral space syndrome, palmar arch injury, and digital ischemia. Lower extremity conditions discussed include arterial thromboembolism, external iliac artery endofibrosis and dissection, adductor canal syndrome, chronic exertional compartment syndrome, popliteal entrapment syndromes, venous insufficiency, and cystic adventitial disease. Other conditions discussed include venous thromboembolism, median arcuate ligament compression, aortopathies, pulmonary hypertension, Bezold-Jarisch reflex, coronary artery disease, coronary anomalies, and high-flow priapism. The authors aim to equip radiologists with essential knowledge to promptly recognize these conditions, thereby facilitating early intervention and improved outcomes. ©RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article. llm_summary: Vascular abnormalities, which are problems with blood vessels, can occur in athletes and range from minor discomfort to life-threatening conditions like sudden cardiac death, making them challenging to diagnose accurately. This comprehensive review examines various blood vessel problems that affect athletes in different parts of the body, including the arms, legs, heart, and lungs, using multiple imaging techniques such as ultrasound, CT scans, MRI scans, and traditional angiography to identify these conditions. The authors describe numerous specific conditions affecting athletes, such as compressed arteries in the upper arms, blood clots in the legs, pinched nerves affecting blood flow, and abnormal coronary arteries that supply blood to the heart. By providing radiologists, who are doctors who specialize in medical imaging, with detailed knowledge about recognizing these vascular problems, the review aims to help doctors diagnose athletes quickly and start treatment early, which can prevent serious complications and improve patient outcomes. This educational resource is particularly important because vascular abnormalities in athletes are less common than muscle and bone injuries, so doctors might not think to look for them without proper training and awareness.

title: Advancing body contouring: A comprehensive review of intramuscular fat grafting techniques, outcomes, and safety considerations.
abstract: Intramuscular fat grafting has emerged as a transformative technique in aesthetic surgery, particularly within modern body contouring procedures where high-definition contouring and selective volume enhancement are desired. While subcutaneous fat grafting remains a foundational approach, intramuscular injection has been suggested to provide superior definition, projection, and dynamic contouring in selected anatomical regions. Nevertheless, its clinical adoption remains controversial due to ongoing concerns regarding safety, variable fat retention, and inconsistent reporting of complications. A structured literature search was conducted in PubMed, ScienceDirect, and the Cochrane Library using database-specific combinations of intramuscular- and fat grafting-related terms, yielding 495 reports. Ultimately, 45 studies met the inclusion criteria and were retrieved. Analysis focused on safety, fat retention, and clinical outcomes. The included studies suggested favorable aesthetic outcomes and generally positive reported satisfaction across selected facial, truncal, and extremity applications, although outcome reporting was heterogeneous and often non-standardized. While animal models present conflicting retention data, clinical series have described acceptable volume persistence in selected settings. Safety appeared to be strongly region-dependent. While intramuscular gluteal injection remains associated with a prohibitive embolic risk, non-gluteal ultrasound-guided applications reported low rates of major complications in the reviewed literature, although the available evidence remains limited. In conclusion, this review summarizes reported intramuscular fat grafting techniques and synthesizes the available evidence on outcomes and region-specific safety considerations. Future studies must focus on comparing this approach to subcutaneous grafting in larger cohorts.© 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd on behalf of British Association of Plastic, Reconstructive and Aesthetic Surgeons.

llm_summary: Intramuscular fat grafting, which involves injecting a patient's own fat directly into muscles rather than just under the skin to reshape the body, has become increasingly popular in cosmetic surgery because it can create sharper definition and better projection in areas like the face and limbs. Researchers reviewed forty-five scientific studies from medical databases to understand how well this technique works, how safe it is, and how long the results last. The studies showed that patients generally felt satisfied with their results and experienced good outcomes in most body areas, though the safety of the procedure depended heavily on where the injection was performed, with buttock injections carrying serious risks of blood clots while other areas proved much safer when guided by ultrasound. The findings suggest that intramuscular fat grafting can be a useful tool for body contouring in carefully selected locations outside the buttocks, but doctors need more research to confirm it works better than the traditional method of injecting fat under the skin. Future studies should directly compare intramuscular fat grafting to subcutaneous fat grafting, or the standard under-the-skin approach, in larger groups of patients to determine which method produces the best and safest results.

title: Nonsystemic Vasculitic Neuropathy Presenting as Inflammatory Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy.
abstract: Nonsystemic vasculitic neuropathy classically presents as a painful asymmetric axonal neuropathy, multiple mononeuropathies or radiculoplexus neuropathy. Demyelinating electrophysiologic features are rare and may lead to misdiagnosis. We describe a patient with biopsy-proven vasculitic neuropathy presenting as a severe symmetric demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy.Clinical, electrophysiologic, imaging, laboratory, and histopathologic findings are presented.A 57-year-old man developed acute ascending weakness, sensory loss, facial weakness, and areflexia following a febrile illness, with initial improvement before developing recurrent neurological decline 6 weeks after initial symptom onset despite treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange. Cerebrospinal fluid protein was elevated. Nerve conduction studies demonstrated prolonged distal motor latencies, slowed conduction velocities, conduction block, and prolonged blink reflex latencies, fulfilling 2021 European Academy of Neurology/Peripheral Nerve Society electrodiagnostic criteria for chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy (CIDP). MRI demonstrated mild but diffuse lumbosacral plexus enlargement and T2 hyperintensity. Sural nerve biopsy ultimately demonstrated evidence of epineurial inflammation and microvasculitis with ischemic nerve injury, accompanied by both increased rates of axonal degeneration (12%) and segmental demyelination (9%) on teased fiber analysis. Treatment with corticosteroids and rituximab resulted in complete neurological recovery.Vasculitic neuropathy may closely mimic CIDP clinically, radiologically, and electrophysiologically. Clues to the vasculitis diagnosis were prominent neuropathic pain, dense denervation on electrophysiology, and poor response to typical CIDP treatment. Peripheral nerve biopsy remains a critical tool in the evaluation of atypical or treatment-refractory inflammatory neuropathies.© 2026 Peripheral Nerve Society.

llm_summary: A rare nerve condition called nonsystemic vasculitic neuropathy, which involves inflammation of blood vessels in nerves, typically shows up as painful, uneven nerve damage, but doctors sometimes miss it when it looks like a more common condition called chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy, or CIDP, which damages the protective coating around nerves. Researchers described a patient who developed sudden weakness, numbness, and facial drooping after a fever, and whose nerve tests showed patterns that perfectly matched CIDP, but a nerve tissue sample revealed the real problem was actually blood vessel inflammation causing nerve injury. The patient had unusual warning signs including severe pain, significant nerve damage on electrical testing, and a poor response to standard CIDP treatments like intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange, which should have worked if he truly had CIDP. When doctors treated him with steroids and rituximab, a medication that targets immune cells, he recovered completely, confirming that the vasculitic neuropathy diagnosis was correct. This case shows that nerve biopsies, which involve taking a small tissue sample to examine under a microscope, remain essential when patients have confusing nerve symptoms.

title: Sustained relief of chronic headache using percutaneous 60-day peripheral nerve stimulation treatment: 12-month results from a multicenter, prospective clinical study.
abstract: The study aimed to assess the long-term durability of pain relief among patients with cervicogenic headache (CGH) or occipital neuralgia (ON) following percutaneous 60-day peripheral nerve stimulation (PNS) treatment.Cervicogenic headache (CGH) and occipital neuralgia (ON) are challenging headache conditions with significant impact on function and quality of life. The present feasibility study initially reported that percutaneous 60-day PNS can reduce headache, facilitating functional improvements such as improved quality of life and reduced neck disability. This work evaluates the durability of clinical outcomes through 12 months within the study cohort.Twenty participants with CGH or ON (and without migraine) received bilateral, percutaneous leads stimulating the occipital nerves. Leads were left indwelling for up to 60 days before being withdrawn. During prospectively defined follow-up through 12 months, participants reported on their occipital pain intensity and pain interference, as well as secondary outcomes.Through 12 months, 82% of participants reported sustained, substantial reductions (≥50%) in pain and/or pain interference. Clinically meaningful changes in secondary outcomes, including pain-related neck disability, impact of headache on daily life, and quality of life, were also observed. Results through 3 months on device effectiveness and safety have been previously published. No new device-related adverse events were reported in the follow-up phase of the study among these participants.A majority of participants with CGH or ON had sustained relief from pain and pain interference, resulting improvements in function, and reductions in disability through 12 months following a percutaneous 60-day PNS treatment without any new device-related adverse events reported after the 3-month follow-up. These findings support the feasibility for 60-day PNS in the treatment of refractory pain due to CGH or ON.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Cervicogenic headache and occipital neuralgia are serious headache conditions that significantly impact people's daily lives and quality of life, making them difficult to treat with standard approaches. Researchers studied twenty patients with these types of headaches who received a temporary electrical nerve stimulation device, which is a thin wire placed near the occipital nerves at the back of the head to deliver mild electrical pulses for up to sixty days before being removed. After twelve months of follow-up, eighty-two percent of the patients reported sustained pain relief of at least fifty percent, along with improvements in neck disability, daily functioning, and overall quality of life. The treatment showed no new safety concerns or device-related side effects during the follow-up period after the initial three months. These results suggest that this temporary nerve stimulation approach may be a feasible option for people suffering from these difficult-to-treat headache conditions, though further research with larger patient groups would help confirm these promising findings.

title: Prognostic value of serial NT-proBNP assay in adults with congenital heart disease and biventricular physiology.
abstract: The available data about the prognostic role of N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) in adults with congenital heart disease (CHD) are derived from small sample size with limited follow-up. The purpose of this study was to assess the role of NT-proBNP assay for prognostication in adults with CHD based on a large cohort.Retrospective cohort study of adults with CHD, biventricular physiology, and systemic morphologic left ventricle who had ≥2 NT-proBNP measurements (2003-2023). Temporal change in NT-proBNP was calculated as relative change from baseline levels (relative Δ_NT-proBNP).Of 3674 patients (age 42 ± 16 years; 47% males), median baseline and follow-up NT-proBNP levels were 178 (72; 539) pg/ml and 236 (103; 854) pg/ml, respectively. The relative Δ_NT-proBNP was 22% (-9, 51), and 2496 (68%) had temporal increase in NT-proBNP levels (i.e., relative Δ_NT-proBNP >0). The correlates of higher baseline NT-proBNP measurement were older age, atrial fibrillation, hepatorenal dysfunction, biventricular systolic dysfunction, and elevated biventricular filling pressures. Overall, 431 (12%) patients died during median follow-up. Both baseline NT-proBNP level and temporal increase in NT-proBNP were associated with all-cause mortality in all patient subgroups. Serial NT-proBNP measurement had superior prognostic value compared to single (baseline) NT-proBNP measurements and had superior prognostic performance compared to conventional clinical indices (echocardiographic indices, invasive hemodynamic indices, exercise test indices).NT-proBNP assay is inexpensive, readily available, and noninvasive, making it ideal for longitudinal monitoring. Further studies are required to determine whether NT-proBNP data can be used to guide therapeutic interventions in this population.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a simple blood test called NT-proBNP, which measures a protein released by the heart under stress, could predict which adults with congenital heart disease (a condition where the heart structure is abnormal from birth) might be at risk of dying. The study looked back at medical records from 3,674 adult patients who had this blood test measured at least twice between 2003 and 2023, tracking how the protein levels changed over time and comparing those changes to patient outcomes. They found that patients whose NT-proBNP levels increased over time had a higher risk of death, and this measurement was more useful for predicting outcomes than looking at a single test result or using other standard heart tests like ultrasounds or exercise tests. This blood test is attractive for doctors because it is inexpensive, easy to perform, and does not require invasive procedures, making it practical for regularly monitoring patients with congenital heart disease over many years. The researchers concluded that while serial NT-proBNP testing shows promise for predicting patient outcomes, more research is needed to determine whether doctors should use these results to guide treatment decisions for this population.

title: Clinical insights into syncope and presyncope during graded exercise testing: A 40,715-test experience.
abstract: Syncope and presyncope during graded exercise testing (GXT) are uncommon but clinically important events that may reflect hemodynamic, autonomic, conductionrelated, or arrhythmic mechanisms. We reviewed all clinically significant syncope and presyncope occurring during non-imaging GXTs performed at Mayo Clinic between January 2006 and December 2010. All clinically significant events underwent detailed chart review incorporating exercise findings, clinical documentation, and longitudinal follow-up to systematically adjudicate the most likely mechanism. Among 40,715 GXTs performed in 33,885 unique patients, eight episodes of syncope (0.20 per 1000 tests) and five episodes of hemodynamically significant presyncope (0.12 per 1000 tests) required test termination. Five additional patients with transient lightheadedness without exercise-induced hypotension or clinically significant arrhythmia and five mechanical treadmill events without hemodynamic compromise were excluded from the primary analysis. Only two events were attributed to a documented arrhythmic mechanism. Most episodes were adjudicated as hemodynamic, autonomic/neurocardiogenic, or indeterminate. Syncope occurred predominantly in younger women and was generally associated with sinus rhythm and hypotensive or autonomic mechanisms, whereas presyncope occurred predominantly in older men with underlying cardiovascular disease, atrial arrhythmias, bradycardia, or chronotropic incompetence. Clinically significant syncope and presyncope during supervised GXT were exceedingly uncommon and were rarely associated with a documented arrhythmic mechanism. These findings support the safety of supervised exercise testing in appropriately monitored settings and improve understanding of the mechanisms underlying these uncommon exercise laboratory events.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Fainting and near-fainting episodes during exercise stress tests, where doctors monitor patients on a treadmill to check heart health, are rare but important events that doctors need to understand. Researchers reviewed over 40,000 exercise stress tests performed at Mayo Clinic between 2006 and 2010 to identify cases where patients fainted or nearly fainted and to figure out what caused these episodes. They found that only 13 significant events occurred out of the 40,715 tests, with fainting happening mostly in younger women and near-fainting occurring more often in older men with existing heart problems. The study showed that most of these episodes were caused by drops in blood pressure or problems with the nervous system's control of the heart, rather than dangerous irregular heartbeats. These results suggest that supervised exercise stress testing is very safe when done in properly monitored medical settings, which should reassure both patients and doctors about the value of this important diagnostic tool.

title: Prescription Trends for Bipolar Disorder With and Without Comorbid Substance Use and Anxiety Disorders: A Global Bipolar Cohort Collaborative Study.
abstract: To investigate pharmacological treatment patterns in individuals with bipolar disorder (BD) with and without comorbid substance use disorder (SUD) and anxiety disorder (AX), we leveraged the Global Bipolar Cohort to analyze cross-regional practices across North America, Europe, and the Pacific.Fourteen cohorts contributed aggregate data on pharmacotherapy, demographics, diagnostic subtypes, and comorbidities. Proportional meta-analyses using generalized linear mixed models were conducted to examine prescription trends and identify clinical differences.The sample (N = 11,521) was 60% female and 84% Caucasian. Participants were categorized into four mutually exclusive groups based on comorbidity status: those with comorbid AX only, comorbid SUD only, both AX and SUD, or neither. The AX+SUD subgroup showed higher rates of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), rapid cycling, obesity, and unemployment, reflecting a more severe clinical profile. Regional variations were notable: North American cohorts reported higher prevalence of AX and SUD than European and Pacific cohorts. Antidepressants use for AX were more common in Europe and the Pacific, while North American prescribing patterns were more variable. Benzodiazepine use was high among individuals with SUD across all regions. Lithium and first-generation antipsychotic prescriptions varied, with higher rates observed in Europe.Findings underscore the heterogeneity of BD and the influence of comorbid AX and SUD on illness burden and treatment. Regional prescribing variations underscore the need for context-specific guidelines. Gaps in data on medication-assisted treatment for SUD point to areas for future research. These insights can support more individualized and effective care for complex BD presentations.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons A/S. Published by John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how doctors prescribe medications differently for people with bipolar disorder, which is a mental health condition involving extreme mood swings, depending on whether patients also struggle with substance abuse or anxiety disorders. The study collected information from over eleven thousand patients across North America, Europe, and the Pacific region to compare treatment patterns and see how comorbidities, or additional conditions occurring alongside the main disorder, affected medication choices. Patients who had both anxiety and substance use disorders showed more severe symptoms including attention problems, trauma-related stress, rapid mood cycling, and higher rates of unemployment compared to those with bipolar disorder alone. The researchers found significant differences in how doctors in different regions prescribed medications, with North American doctors using more antidepressants variably while European doctors prescribed them more consistently, and benzodiazepines, which are calming medications, being widely used for patients with substance abuse issues everywhere. These findings suggest that doctors need region-specific treatment guidelines tailored to local practices and that more research is needed on medication-assisted treatments for substance abuse in bipolar disorder patients.

title: Food and Drug Administration-Approved Fecal Microbiota-Based Therapies for Recurrent Clostridioides difficile Infection.
abstract: Recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection remains common despite optimized antibiotic therapy. Two Food and Drug Administration-approved donor-derived fecal microbiota-based products, fecal microbiota, live-jslm (Rebyota / RBL) and fecal microbiota spores, live-brpk (Vowst / VOS) reduce recurrence when administered after completion of standard antibiotics. This review summarizes the clinical development programs supporting these products, including pivotal randomized trials, open-label extensions, durability data, safety outcomes, and emerging real-world evidence. We also discuss patient selection, timing after antibiotics, diagnostic considerations, and practical implementation. These therapies represent standardized, evidence-based approaches to restoring colonization resistance and preventing recurrent infection in appropriately selected adults.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. The Food and Drug Administration approved two new treatments made from donated healthy gut bacteria that are given to patients after they finish their standard antibiotics to help restore the balance of good bacteria in their digestive system. These two products, called Rebyota and Vowst, were tested in clinical trials and shown to significantly reduce the chances that the infection would return in patients who received them. The review examined all the evidence from these trials, including how long the treatments worked, how safe they were, and real-world results from patients who actually received the therapies outside of controlled research settings. These standardized, science-backed treatments offer doctors a proven way to help carefully selected adult patients rebuild their gut bacteria and prevent the infection from coming back again.

title: Evolution of Achilles Tendon Repair: From Open Surgery to Percutaneous Techniques.
abstract: This article examines the evolution of Achilles tendon repair, focusing on minimally invasive and percutaneous techniques that reduce complications and improve recovery. These approaches emphasize preserving anatomic structures like the paratenon and sural nerve while optimizing biomechanical repair strength. Modern suture configurations enhance stability, enabling early mobilization and better functional outcomes. Clinical evidence shows minimally invasive methods offer comparable or superior results to open surgery, with fewer wound complications and faster return to activity, though sural nerve injury remains a potential risk. These advancements reflect a balance between reduced surgical morbidity and improved patient outcomes.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Achilles tendon injuries are common and serious problems that affect how people walk and move, making it important to find better ways to repair them. Researchers examined how surgical techniques for fixing Achilles tendons have changed over time, moving from traditional open surgery to newer minimally invasive methods that use smaller cuts and special instruments. The newer techniques work by protecting important structures like nerves and surrounding tissue while using modern suture patterns, or stitching methods, that keep the repair strong enough to allow patients to start moving their legs earlier in recovery. Studies show that these minimally invasive approaches produce results that are just as good as or better than traditional open surgery, with fewer wound problems and faster return to normal activities, though there is still a small risk of nerve injury. These advances represent an important shift in how doctors repair Achilles tendons, balancing the goal of reducing surgical damage to the body with the need to help patients recover better and faster.

title: Real-world implementation of a pre-consultation patient educational tool for intermediate risk prostate cancer.
abstract: Prostate Cancer (PCa) decision-making requires patients to understand their diagnosis and therapeutic options, balancing care nuances and risk-to-benefit profiles. The complexity of information and a wide range of treatments often exceed what can be covered in consultation. Our team developed a PCa Educational Tool to enhance patient understanding and support decision-making process.The PCa Educational Tool was designed using plain language principles and evidence-based content. The tool was distributed automatically to newly diagnosed intermediate-risk PCa patients. A post-use questionnaire assessed usability, satisfaction, and perceived educational value. Qualitative feedback was categorized by sentiment and themes. Treatment selection was explored between sequential cohorts before and after implementation.A total of 395 patients received the tool, and 79.7% completed the questionnaire. Among respondents, 88.1% felt more prepared for discussion with their care team, and 74.8% indicated improved understanding of their diagnosis. Satisfaction rates were high, with 93.9% of respondents recommending the tool to other patients. Qualitative analysis revealed positive feedback on the tool's comprehensiveness and format, while highlighting other areas for improvement. Exploratory comparison of treatment selection showed statistically significant differences between the sequential cohorts, with a slight increase selection of brachytherapy and focal therapies.PCa Educational Tool improved patient understanding and preparedness for consultation with the care team. In exploratory analysis, its use is correlated with a statistically significant shift in treatment choices in sequential cohorts (p = 0.048). The process was automated and proved to seamlessly integrate into our clinical workflow. Future steps include tool refinement based on patient feedback.© 2026 The Authors.

llm_summary: Researchers examined whether an educational tool could help patients newly diagnosed with intermediate-risk prostate cancer, which is cancer that has moderate chances of spreading, understand their diagnosis and treatment options before meeting with their doctors. The team created a simple, easy-to-understand educational tool using plain language and sent it automatically to nearly four hundred newly diagnosed patients, then asked them questions about whether the tool was helpful and easy to use. Almost nine out of ten patients who used the tool said they felt more prepared to talk with their care team, and three-quarters reported better understanding of their diagnosis, with over ninety percent recommending it to other patients. The study found that after the tool was introduced, there was a noticeable shift in which treatments patients chose, with slightly more patients selecting brachytherapy, a type of radiation therapy placed inside the body, and focal therapies, which target only the cancer rather than the whole prostate. The researchers plan to improve the tool based on patient suggestions and continue studying how it affects patient care, since the automated system worked smoothly within the existing clinic workflow.

title: Message Received? Applicant Insights on Preference Signals in General Surgery Residency Recruitment.
abstract: We aimed to understand general surgery applicants' experiences with and attitudes toward preference signaling.Qualitative analysis of de-identified transcripts from semi-structured interviews of general surgery residency applicants was performed.A general surgery residency program at an academic hospital in the United States.All applicants to one general surgery residency program in the 2024 to 2025 recruitment cycle were invited to participate. Twenty-seven applicants participated in semi-structured interviews (59% female, 63% MD graduates, 11% DO graduates, 26% international medical school graduates).While applicants decided where to signal differently, applicants noted that they signaled across a range of program competitiveness and made strategic choices based on interest versus likelihood of matching. While applicants highlighted the importance of a good advisor, they noted that disagreements were common between advisors regarding signaling strategies. Applicants additionally noted a disparity in advising for IMG and DO applicants, as their schools often did not have surgery-specific advisors or a track record of matching into surgical specialties. Applicants focused on several signaling pitfalls, including difficulty judging their competitiveness and determining where they would "fit" before their interviews. While applicants did not expect to receive interview offers from non-signaled programs, they found these interviews could go 2 ways: either non-signaled programs were a good fit, or they experienced quasi-adversarial interactions about their potential lack of interest. With respect to future changes, applicants wanted more transparency regarding each program's screening process and felt that signal number changes should be data-driven to ensure applicants receive enough interviews to match.Applicants had varied experiences with signaling, reporting different allocation strategies and guidance from advisors. Applicants highlighted a need for transparency regarding how applicants should signal and how programs interpret signals. This transparency can break down the hidden curriculum of signaling, improving applicant trust in the recruitment process.Copyright © 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined how medical school graduates applying for general surgery residency programs experience and feel about preference signals, which are messages applicants send to programs indicating their interest in matching there. The study involved interviews with twenty-seven applicants to one surgery residency program, with participants representing different educational backgrounds including medical school graduates, osteopathic graduates, and international medical school graduates. The applicants reported using different strategies for where to send their preference signals, often choosing programs based on both genuine interest and realistic chances of being accepted, though they struggled to judge their own competitiveness and find programs where they would truly fit. Applicants also noted that getting advice about signaling was inconsistent and sometimes contradictory, with international and osteopathic graduates particularly lacking specialized guidance since their schools often had no track record in surgery placements. To improve the process, applicants called for programs to be more transparent about how they screen applicants and suggested that the number of allowed signals should be based on data to ensure everyone gets enough interview offers to successfully match into a program.

title: Unique presentation of urosymphyseal fistula and conservative management.
abstract: A urosymphyseal fistula is an abnormal connection between the lower urinary tract (typically bladder or proximal urethra) and pubic symphysis. This is an uncommon late complication of prostate cancer treatment, often occurring after pelvic radiation and urethral instrumentation. We report a 79-year-old man who, after external radiotherapy, salvage brachytherapy, and transurethral bladder neck incision, developed a urosymphyseal fistula with urinary tracking into the anterior thigh compartment. Given comorbidities, he was managed conservatively with urinary diversion, percutaneous drainage, and antibiotic therapy. Serial imaging demonstrated nonoperative resolution. This case highlights an unusual clinical presentation and suggests selected patients may avoid extirpative surgery.© 2026 The Authors. Published by Elsevier Inc.

llm_summary: A urosymphyseal fistula is a rare abnormal tunnel that forms between the bladder or urethra and the pubic bone, and it can develop years after men receive radiation treatment for prostate cancer. Doctors reported the case of a 79-year-old man who developed this condition after undergoing external radiation therapy, internal radiation implants, and a surgical procedure to open his bladder neck, which caused urine to leak into the tissue of his front thigh. Instead of performing major surgery to remove the affected tissue, the medical team chose to treat him with a catheter to redirect urine away from the bladder, a drainage tube placed through the skin to remove fluid buildup, and antibiotics to prevent infection. Imaging scans taken over time showed that the fistula healed on its own without the need for surgery, suggesting that some patients with this serious complication may recover without having to undergo extensive operations. This case demonstrates that doctors should consider conservative treatment options for carefully selected patients with this rare condition rather than automatically recommending surgery.

title: Grading and Reporting of Graft-versus-Host Disease in the Modern Era.
abstract: Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) continues to be a major cause of morbidity after allogeneic stem cell transplantation. This article summarizes current approaches to grading and reporting gastrointestinal GVHD while outlining key histopathological features, diagnostic thresholds, and interpretive challenges. It emphasizes the need for clinicopathologic correlation and awareness of common mimickers, and the growing role of plasma biomarkers in risk stratification/assessment. Emerging tools in artificial intelligence-enabled digital pathology and standardized reporting practices aim to improve diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical relevance in the management of GVHD in modern practice.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Graft-versus-host disease, a serious condition where immune cells from a donor attack a patient's own body after a stem cell transplant, remains a major problem that causes significant suffering and complications in transplant patients. This article reviews the current best practices for identifying and grading gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease, which affects the digestive system, by explaining the key tissue changes doctors look for under a microscope and the thresholds they use to diagnose it. The authors highlight important challenges in diagnosis, including the need to compare what doctors see in the lab with what patients experience clinically and the importance of recognizing other conditions that can look similar to graft-versus-host disease. The research emphasizes that blood tests measuring specific proteins, called biomarkers, are becoming increasingly valuable tools for predicting which patients are at higher risk and for tracking how well treatments are working. Modern technology such as artificial intelligence-powered digital pathology and standardized reporting systems are emerging as promising approaches to make diagnoses more accurate, consistent, and useful for doctors managing patients with this serious transplant complication.

title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.
abstract: Anti-Spike monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) progressively lost efficacy during the COVID-19 pandemic due to the emergence and predominance of resistant SARS-CoV-2 variants. By contrast, high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) collected from vaccinated donors recently recovered from infection provides a polyclonal source of antibodies that remains effective in clearing SARS-CoV-2 in immunosuppressed patients, unable to mount an adequate immune response against the virus. We conducted a systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis to examine the effect of CCP in immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following mAb therapy, and to evaluate possible biological factors associated with a favourable outcome. Electronic databases were searched for studies published from January 2020 to January 2026. All studies including eligible cases were considered in the systematic review. Unpublished cases were also collected from investigators of the selected studies. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 cases from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included. In 33 out of 47 patients (70.2%) with a mAb-resistant infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. In logistic regression, total CCP volume transfused was positively associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance. In conclusion, CCP transfusion was associated with SARS-CoV-2 clearance in persistently positive immunocompromised patients following failure of anti-Spike mAb therapy.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd. llm_summary: Researchers examined whether a blood treatment called convalescent plasma, which contains antibodies from people who recovered from COVID-19, could help immunocompromised patients whose infections had stopped responding to monoclonal antibody drugs, which are laboratory-made proteins designed to fight the virus. The team conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis, meaning they searched medical databases for all relevant studies published between January 2020 and January 2026 and combined data from 47 patients, including 30 from published studies and 17 from unpublished cases. The results showed that about 70 percent of patients who had failed monoclonal antibody treatment successfully cleared their virus after receiving convalescent plasma transfusions, with patients typically receiving an average of 2. 7 units of the plasma. The study found that patients who received larger total volumes of convalescent plasma were more likely to successfully eliminate their virus, suggesting that the amount of treatment matters for achieving a positive outcome.

title: Comparison of Factors Associated With 30-Day and 90-Day Readmission Among a Global Cohort of Patients Hospitalised With Cirrhosis.
abstract: It remains unclear whether different factors influence 30- and 90-day readmission rates. We identified predictors of 90-day mortality in a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis.Variables associated with 30- and 90-day post-discharge readmission, liver transplantation (LT), and mortality were compared in prospectively enrolled, non-electively hospitalised adult patients with cirrhosis.We enrolled 4208 patients from 125 centres across 37 countries. Alcohol-related liver disease was the most common aetiology of cirrhosis (40%), followed by hepatitis B virus infection (21%); 47% were readmitted, 8% received liver transplantation (LT), and 23% died within 90 days post-discharge. In multivariable analysis, country income was significantly associated with both 30- and 90-day readmission rates, the receipt of LT, and mortality within 30 and 90 days post-discharge (all p-values < 0.001). Independent predictors of higher rates of 30- and 90-day readmissions, respectively, were disease severity (p < 0.001, p = 0.003), prior ascites (p = 0.025, p = 0.016), prior hospitalisation (p < 0.001), hyponatremia (p < 0.001, p = 0.008), and in-hospital vasopressor use (p = 0.002, p = 0.011). Prior variceal bleeding independently predicted higher 90-day readmission rates, whereas age, disease severity, mechanical ventilation, and in-hospital vasopressor use (all, p < 0.001) increased odds of 30- and 90-day post-discharge death. Additionally, admission (p = 0.011) and nosocomial (p = 0.022) infections increased the odds of 90-day post-discharge death.In a global cohort of hospitalised patients with cirrhosis, patients in high-income countries exhibited the highest rates of 30- and 90-day readmission, alongside lower mortality rates and a higher incidence of LT. Variables that predict 30-day readmission also predicted 90-day readmission. Understanding these disparities is essential for achieving health equity.© 2026 John Wiley & Sons A/S. llm_summary: Researchers examined what factors lead patients with cirrhosis, a serious liver disease, to be readmitted to the hospital within 30 and 90 days after discharge, since understanding these patterns could help doctors prevent future hospitalizations. The study followed 4,208 patients from 125 hospitals across 37 countries who were admitted to the hospital with cirrhosis, tracking which patients returned to the hospital and which factors predicted their readmission. The researchers found that nearly half of the patients were readmitted within 90 days, and that factors like disease severity, low sodium levels in the blood, previous fluid buildup in the abdomen, and the need for blood pressure medications during hospitalization all increased the risk of readmission. Importantly, patients in wealthy countries had higher readmission rates but lower death rates and more access to liver transplants, suggesting that healthcare resources and access to care play a major role in patient outcomes. These findings highlight that the same warning signs predict both early and late readmissions, and that addressing health inequalities between rich and poor countries is essential for improving survival and quality of life for cirrhosis patients worldwide.

title: Back to Biochemistry: Evaluation for and Prognostic Significance of SDH Mutations in Paragangliomas and Pheochromocytomas.
abstract: There is increasing recognition of the high prevalence of hereditary predisposition syndromes in patients diagnosed with paraganglioma/pheochromocytoma. It is widely acknowledged that germline pathogenic alterations of the succinate dehydrogenase complex genes (SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2) contribute to the pathogenesis of most of these tumors. llm_summary: Many people diagnosed with a type of tumor called paraganglioma or pheochromocytoma actually have inherited genetic conditions that make them more likely to develop these cancers. Researchers examined how mutations in a group of genes related to a cellular energy-producing system called the succinate dehydrogenase complex contribute to the development of these tumors. The study found that changes in genes like SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, and SDHAF2 are responsible for most cases of these tumors and that these genetic changes are passed down through families in predictable patterns. Understanding how these genetic mutations damage the energy-producing system in cells helps doctors better diagnose patients and predict how serious their condition might be. This research highlights the importance of genetic testing for patients with these tumors so that doctors can identify at-risk family members and provide better treatment and monitoring options.

title: OCT-defined optic atrophy thresholds are associated with blunted optic nerve swelling in recurrent optic neuritis.
abstract: Acute optic neuritis (ON) can be associated with optic disc edema which can be quantified by optical coherence tomography (OCT) peripapillary retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) measurements. In patients with recurrent visual symptoms, objective measures can confirm a new clinical attack. Optic atrophy may preclude RNFL swelling during recurrent ON, but this has not been systematically evaluated.Patients with recurrent ipsilateral ON with OCT within 2 weeks of symptoms were retrospectively identified from 8 international centers.We identified 112 patients (MOGAD, 45[40%]; MS, 36[32%], NMOSD, 20[18%], idiopathic ON, 11[10%]) with 137 episodes of recurrent ON (median age, 39 years [range 12-78]; female sex, 81 [72%]). Of patients with macular ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer (GCIPL) measures during acute recurrent ON, those with preserved GCIPL (≥65 μm, n=36) showed greater RNFL thickness (mean 108 μm [65-368], p<0.0001) than those with thin GCIPL (<65μm, n=30; mean 65μm [50-84]). Higher RNFL thickness measurements, which can be consistent with RNFL swelling, (≥15 µm above GCIPL) occurred in 21/36 (58%) patients with GCIPL ≥65 µm vs 5/30 (17%) patients with GCIPL <65µm (p<0.001).Patients with severe optic atrophy may have limited optic nerve swelling during acute ON. Ganglion cell layer thickness can serve as a surrogate marker for optic atrophy during early acute ON. We identified quantitative thresholds (GCIPL [<65μm] or prior RNFL [<70μm]) at which optic nerve swelling is unlikely to occur during recurrent acute ON. This is important for objective assessment of ON in clinical practice and clinical trials.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.

llm_summary: Researchers examined patients who experienced repeated episodes of optic neuritis, which is inflammation of the nerve that carries vision from the eye to the brain, to understand how previous damage affects new attacks. The study looked at 112 patients from eight international medical centers who had recurrent optic neuritis and had eye imaging scans taken within two weeks of their symptoms appearing. The researchers found that patients whose eye nerve tissue was already thinned from previous damage showed much less swelling during new attacks compared to patients with healthier nerve tissue, with only 17 percent of those with severe thinning showing significant swelling versus 58 percent of those with preserved tissue. The study identified specific measurement thresholds showing that when the inner layer of the retina measures less than 65 micrometers thick, doctors should not expect to see nerve swelling during acute attacks, which helps explain why some patients may not show obvious signs of a new attack on imaging. These findings are important because they help doctors and researchers better understand how to objectively confirm new optic neuritis attacks in patients who have experienced previous episodes, which matters for both clinical care and for designing fair research studies.

title: Patient Safety in Obstetric Anesthesiology: Current Challenges and Prevention Strategies.
abstract: Administration of anesthetic care in the peripartum period represents numerous areas where vigilance in clinical care and implementation of systematic safety measures are needed to improve maternal outcomes. Obstetric anesthesia care often necessitates expeditious intervention in an environment where both maternal and fetal conditions change rapidly. A thorough understanding of the risks of each intervention as well as best practices to improve maternal safety are critical to optimize patient outcomes. Continued reassessment of protocols and implementation of new evidence and consensus-based guidelines are needed to continually enhance maternal safety in this complex health care environment.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Inc. llm_summary: Anesthesia care during pregnancy and childbirth is a critical area where safety improvements are needed to protect mothers and their babies. The authors reviewed current challenges in obstetric anesthesia, which is the medical care that helps manage pain during pregnancy and delivery when conditions can change very quickly. They emphasized that doctors need to understand the risks of different treatments and follow best practices to keep mothers safe during this complex medical situation. The research highlights that healthcare teams must regularly check and update their safety procedures based on the latest medical evidence and expert recommendations. These ongoing improvements in protocols and guidelines are essential to continue making childbirth safer for all mothers receiving anesthetic care.

title: Level of Agreement in Perceived Improvement in a Cohort of Parent-Child Dyads Following an Interdisciplinary Pain Management Program.
abstract: This study assessed the level of agreement of perceived improvements among pediatric patients with chronic pain and their parents following an interdisciplinary pain management program. This is a retrospective chart review of a heterogeneous group of pediatric patients with chronic pain who completed an interdisciplinary pain management program (IPMP) and their parents (N = 172 pairs). The IPMP took place in an outpatient pain management center affiliated with an academic rehabilitation hospital. The outcome measures included the Multidimensional Patient Impression of Change (MPIC) and the MPIC parent version were administered post-treatment. The levels of agreement on the MPIC were analyzed between child and parent using the free-marginal kappa statistic. The majority of both the parents and the children evaluated the patients to be much or very much improved in six of the eight domains assessed. The levels of agreement in the ratings were fair to moderate among the patient-parent dyads. Parents endorsed significantly higher levels of improved overall pain and mood than their child did, whereas the patients reported greater levels of improved ability to cope with pain than their parents did. Both the patients and their parents reported high levels of perceived improvement following the IPMP. However, there were some differences in their ratings of improvements in overall pain, mood, and ability to cope with pain. Given that some of the perceptions were discrepant, it is recommended that feedback be obtained from the patient and their parent.© 2026 The Author(s). llm_summary: Researchers examined whether children with long-term pain and their parents agreed on how much the children improved after completing a special pain management program that uses multiple types of treatment like physical therapy and counseling. The study looked back at medical records for 172 pairs of children and parents who had finished this outpatient program at a rehabilitation hospital and asked them both to rate their perceived improvements across eight different areas. Both the children and parents reported that most patients got much better or very much better in six of the eight areas measured, but the level of agreement between what children said and what parents said was only fair to moderate. Parents thought the children's overall pain and mood improved more than the children themselves believed, while children felt they had improved more in their ability to handle pain than their parents thought. Because children and parents sometimes saw improvements differently, doctors should make sure to ask both the child and the parent for their opinions when deciding if the treatment worked well.

title: AI scribe functions in psychiatric practice: clinical oversight, consent, and regulation.
abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) documentation tools, known as AI scribes, have entered psychiatric clinical practice, bundling at least three operations into a single workflow, without sufficient attention to the differences among them. In this Personal View, we argue that AI-generated clinical narrative (history of present illness), AI-generated clinical observation (mental status examination), and AI-generated diagnostic reasoning (assessment and plan) are functionally distinct operations that stand in qualitatively different relationships to their shared input, with distinct failure modes and oversight demands. We describe why psychiatric practice exposes these distinctions with particular clarity and examine their implications for liability, informed consent, and regulation. Psychiatry is uniquely positioned to surface distinctions among these operations because of the therapeutic and legal weight of word choice, the unnarrated structure of the mental status exam, and the formulation-driven nature of diagnostic reasoning. We offer provisional practice considerations for clinicians currently using these AI scribes and call for the field to build frameworks that reflect the different claims these AI scribes' outputs make.Copyright © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. llm_summary: Artificial intelligence tools that automatically write down what happens during psychiatric appointments, called AI scribes, are now being used in mental health clinics but they bundle together three very different tasks without enough careful oversight. The researchers examined how these AI tools perform three distinct functions: writing down what patients say about their symptoms, observing and describing the patient's mental state, and making diagnostic decisions about what might be wrong and how to treat it. They argue that psychiatry is the perfect field to highlight why these three functions are fundamentally different from each other because words matter so much in mental health treatment, both for helping patients and for legal reasons. The authors point out that each of these three functions can fail in different ways and requires different kinds of supervision, informed consent from patients, and government regulation to keep people safe. The researchers call for the medical field to create new guidelines that recognize these important differences and treat each function separately rather than bundling them all together as one tool.
